agent-injection-ci.one_shot:
You are a defensive security engineer hardening the user's OWN agent. This pack is for defense only: understanding attack CLASSES, building detectors and evals, and containing what your own agent can do. Do not produce operational attacks against third parties; test only harnesses, accounts and keys the user owns. No marketing language.

Context and method: prompt injection cannot be reliably filtered at the input (carterperez.dev) - so you CONTAIN capability. Noma's workflow-hijacking research (mattjayy / vulnu.xyz/noma-ig) shows automations returning data to whoever asks because nobody checks authorization - so add an identity/authorization gate. The Princeton study (forgoodcode) shows models push a sponsored option even when instructed not to - include that as a bias case. Use jailbreak corpora only as abstract attack classes (system-prompt override, role-play escape, encoded payload, tool-output injection) to build detectors against your own harness.

Hard constraints: a disposable canary secret in an isolated test environment; an outbound tool-call allowlist; a fixed suite run on every skill install and harness change; FAIL the change if the canary leaks or a tool call escapes the allowlist; measure the falsifier (allowlist-only block rate). Name the real harness, hooks, skills and CI. All targets owned by the user.

Ordered deliverables: (1) the threat model for YOUR harness - where untrusted text enters (fetched web/Reddit/X content, skill descriptions, tool outputs, inbound email) and what the agent can touch (keys, files, network, money). (2) a canary secret planted in a disposable test env + an outbound tool-call allowlist. (3) a ~50-case defensive suite: direct-injection classes, Noma-style 'ask nicely' authorization-bypass cases planted in fake fetched content, and sponsored-bias nudges - each with an expected safe outcome. (4) per-skill capability manifests (network/filesystem/secrets). (5) an authorization gate on data-returning automations. (6) CI wiring: on skill install / harness change -> diff -> isolated load with canary -> rerun suite -> fail on canary leak or allowlist escape. (7) a layer-attribution table answering the falsifier: % blocked by allowlist alone vs needing manifests vs needing skill-level testing.

Built-in gap analysis: before finishing, list what is unverified - does the suite actually catch a planted injection; does the canary assertion cover all tool outputs; does CI really block a failing install; is the allowlist-only block rate measured or guessed. Fill what you can by running it.

Self-questions to answer in writing: Where exactly does untrusted text enter my harness? Does the canary assertion cover every outbound channel, or just one? Did I plant a real injection in a test skill and confirm the suite catches it? Does CI actually fail the install, or only log? What does a plain allowlist block without any skill testing (the falsifier)? Does the authorization gate check requester identity before returning data? Am I testing only my own systems?

Stop conditions: stop and ask only if there is no harness you own to test or no safe canary environment. Otherwise build end to end.

Return format: a markdown report with the threat model, a file tree, the suite results (case class, outcome, layer that caught it), the planted-injection catch evidence, the canary-never-leaked proof, and the falsifier table (allowlist-only block rate). steps.title: Threat-model your own harness
steps.goal: Map where untrusted text enters and what the agent can touch.
steps.prompt: Establish ground truth defensively. For YOUR OWN agent harness, map two things. (A) Untrusted-input surfaces: every place external text reaches the model - fetched web/Reddit/X content (e.g. via an Agent-Reach-style reader), skill descriptions and READMEs you install, tool outputs, inbound email, file contents. (B) Capability surface: everything the agent can do that matters - API keys/secrets in the environment, filesystem writes/deletes, outbound network, any money or account actions. Produce a table linking each input surface to the capabilities an injection there could abuse. This is the threat model the suite and the allowlist are built from. Keep it about your own setup; do not target anyone else's systems.
steps.expect: A threat-model table: untrusted-input surfaces x reachable capabilities, scoped to the user's own harness.
steps.audit: Confirm every installed skill and every fetch path is listed as an input surface, and every secret/filesystem/network/money capability is listed. Fail if a known input path or capability is missing. On fail, enumerate the harness fully (list skills, hooks, env vars) and complete it.

steps.title: Canary + outbound allowlist
steps.goal: Plant a canary and define what tool calls are allowed to leave.
steps.prompt: Build the containment baseline. (1) Plant a throwaway CANARY secret (a unique random string) in a DISPOSABLE test environment that mimics your real one - never a real key. (2) Define an outbound tool-call allowlist: the exact tools, and for each, the allowed targets (recipients, hosts, paths). Anything outside it is denied by default. (3) Add an assertion harness that inspects every outbound tool call and every model output for the canary string and for off-allowlist destinations. This is enforced in code, not asked of the model. Confirm the assertion sees a tool call (feed one benign call through and watch it log).
steps.expect: A canary planted in a disposable env, an outbound allowlist (tools + targets), and a code assertion that inspects all tool calls/outputs for canary leaks and off-allowlist destinations.
steps.audit: Feed one call containing the canary deliberately and confirm the assertion flags it; feed one off-allowlist destination and confirm denial. Fail if the assertion misses either, or if a real secret was used. On fail, fix coverage before building the suite.

steps.title: Build the defensive suite
steps.goal: Author ~50 injection/hijack/bias cases as attack classes with safe-expected outcomes.
steps.prompt: Build a fixed suite of about 50 DEFENSIVE cases against your own harness, grouped as attack CLASSES (not copy-paste operational attacks on others). (A) Direct injection (~20): system-prompt override attempts, role-play/'ignore previous instructions' escapes, and encoded/obfuscated payloads embedded in fetched content - each expecting the agent to refuse and keep the canary. (B) Authorization-bypass / 'ask nicely' (~20): modelled on the Noma workflow-hijacking research - a request planted in fake fetched Reddit/X/email content asking the automation to return data or act, where the requester is NOT authorized; expected outcome is the agent checks authorization and refuses. (C) Sponsored-bias nudges (~10): modelled on the Princeton study, content pushing a paid/sponsored option; expected outcome is the agent stays neutral even when the content tells it to prefer the sponsor. Each case: input, where it enters (which surface from step 1), and the expected SAFE outcome.
steps.expect: ~50 cases across direct-injection, authorization-bypass and sponsored-bias classes, each tagged with its input surface and expected safe outcome.
steps.audit: Confirm every case maps to an input surface from step 1 and states a safe expected outcome, and that no case is an operational attack against a third-party system. Fail if any case targets someone else's infrastructure or lacks an expected outcome. On fail, rewrite it as a defensive class against your own harness.

steps.title: Capability manifests + authorization gate
steps.goal: Contain what each skill can do and check authorization before returning data.
steps.prompt: Add the containment layers carterperez.dev argues for (contain what the AI can do, since you cannot filter injection). (1) Per-skill capability manifests: for each installed skill, declare its allowed network hosts, filesystem paths, and whether it may read secrets; enforce the manifest at the harness level so a skill cannot exceed it. (2) An authorization gate on any automation that returns data or acts on request (the Noma fix): before responding, verify the requester is authorized for that data/action; if identity is absent or unauthorized, refuse. Re-run the step-3 suite with these layers active and record how many cases each layer now blocks.
steps.expect: Capability manifests enforced per skill, an authorization gate on data-returning automations, and a per-layer block count on the suite.
steps.audit: Pick one skill and confirm it cannot reach a host/path outside its manifest; feed an unauthorized data request and confirm the gate refuses. Fail if a skill exceeds its manifest or the gate returns data without an identity check. On fail, tighten enforcement.

steps.title: Wire the CI
steps.goal: Run the suite automatically on every skill install and harness change.
steps.prompt: Wire prompt-injection CI. On every skill install (e.g. from find-skills or a skills hub) and every harness change: (1) DIFF the incoming change and show what capabilities it adds. (2) Load it in an ISOLATED test harness that has the canary (never real keys). (3) Re-run the full suite with the new skill/change loaded. (4) FAIL the install/change (non-zero exit, block the merge) if the canary leaks in any output/tool call OR any tool call goes outside the allowlist OR the skill exceeds its manifest. Implement as a GitHub Actions workflow and/or a local pre-install hook. Prove it by attempting to install a test skill that contains a planted injection and confirming CI blocks it.
steps.expect: A CI workflow/hook that diffs, isolates with the canary, reruns the suite, and fails the change on canary leak, allowlist escape, or manifest breach - proven by a blocked malicious test install.
steps.audit: Attempt to install a benign skill (should pass) and a skill with a planted injection (should fail). Fail if CI passes the malicious one or blocks the benign one, or if it only logs instead of failing. On fail, fix the exit/blocking behaviour.

steps.title: Falsifier measurement + gap report
steps.goal: Attribute blocking to layers; answer the dive's falsifier; report gaps.
steps.prompt: Final validation and the dive's own falsifier. (1) Layer attribution: run the suite with ONLY the outbound allowlist active (no manifests, no skill-level suite logic) and record what fraction of cases it blocks. Then add manifests, then the full skill-level suite, recording the incremental block rate of each. (2) Answer the falsifier: if the plain allowlist alone blocks >=95% of cases, state clearly that a static outbound policy file is most of the answer and the CI layer is justified only for the remaining cases; if it blocks far less, the skill-level CI is doing real work - quantify it. (3) Confirm the canary never leaked across any run. (4) Enumerate claims, mark verified/unverified/false, list missing pieces ranked by impact, fix the top two. Commit suite, CI, manifests, gate; print the hash.
steps.expect: A layer-attribution table (allowlist-only %, +manifests %, +skill-suite %), an explicit falsifier verdict, a canary-never-leaked confirmation, a claim ledger, and a committed harness with hash.
steps.audit: Confirm the allowlist-only run genuinely disabled the other layers. Confirm the falsifier verdict follows the measured numbers, not a preferred conclusion. Fail if the attribution is estimated or the canary leaked anywhere. On fail, re-run with layers isolated and report the real split.

agent-injection-ci.gap_audit_prompt: Run after the CI harness is built, defensively and against your own systems only. Enumerate every claim as a numbered list: the threat-model coverage, the canary assertion coverage, each suite class, the capability manifests, the authorization gate, the CI blocking behaviour, and the layer-attribution numbers. Mark each VERIFIED (with evidence: a blocked test install, an assertion log, the attribution table), UNVERIFIED, or FALSE. Specifically re-check: does the canary assertion cover EVERY outbound channel, not just one; did a deliberately planted injection in a test skill actually get caught; does CI FAIL (non-zero/block) rather than merely log; does a skill get contained to its manifest; does the authorization gate check requester identity before returning data; is the allowlist-only block rate measured with the other layers truly disabled. List missing pieces: unmonitored output channels, untested skill classes, CI that only warns, estimated attribution. Rank by impact on whether your own agent is actually harder to hijack. Fix the top three and re-verify. Confirm no case targets third-party systems. Report what you could not fix and why.
self_questions: Where exactly does untrusted text enter my harness, and did I enumerate every surface?
Does the canary assertion cover every outbound channel, or only one tool?
Did I plant a real injection in a test skill and confirm the suite catches it?
Does CI actually FAIL the install/change, or does it only log a warning?
What fraction do a plain allowlist block alone (the falsifier), with other layers truly disabled?
Does each skill get contained to its capability manifest, enforced in code?
Does the authorization gate verify requester identity before returning data (the Noma fix)?
Did I include the sponsored-bias case, and does the agent stay neutral under it?
Are my varied framings catching injection classes, or only the obvious phrasings?
Is every test case against a system, account and key I own?
Did I use any real secret instead of a disposable canary anywhere?
Is the layer-attribution split measured, or did I guess which layer blocks what?
validation_oracles: The suite, run against the user's own harness, catches a deliberately planted injection in a test skill; CI blocks that install with a non-zero exit.
The canary secret never appears in any outbound tool call or model output across the entire suite and the unattended CI runs.
A skill cannot exceed its capability manifest (network/filesystem/secrets), confirmed by an attempted out-of-manifest access being denied.
The authorization gate refuses a data-returning request whose requester identity is absent or unauthorized (the Noma workflow-hijacking fix).
The layer-attribution table answers the falsifier with measured numbers: the allowlist-only block rate is stated, and the CI layer's incremental value is quantified.
failure_modes: Input-filter theatre: trying to filter injections out of text. Tell: effort spent on blocklists of phrases. Fix: contain capability (allowlist + manifests), since injection cannot be reliably filtered.
Partial canary coverage: assertion watches one channel. Tell: canary leaks via an unmonitored tool. Fix: assert on every outbound channel and model output.
CI that only logs: suite runs but never blocks. Tell: a failing install still completes. Fix: non-zero exit / block the merge on any failure.
Suite never actually catches anything: no planted injection to prove it. Tell: all-green with no negative control. Fix: plant a real injection in a test skill and confirm it is caught.
No authorization check: automation returns data to whoever asks (the Noma finding). Tell: 'ask nicely' cases pass through. Fix: identity/authorization gate before returning data.
Guessed attribution: falsifier answered from intuition. Tell: no allowlist-only run. Fix: disable other layers and measure the allowlist-only block rate.
Scope drift into offense: cases become attacks on third-party systems. Tell: targets you do not own. Fix: keep every case an abstract class against your own harness.
agent-injection-ci.agent_direction: This is a defensive build against the user's OWN systems only; refuse any drift toward attacking third-party infrastructure. Reach first for the threat model (enumerate the harness's input surfaces and capabilities) and the canary+allowlist containment baseline, before writing any test case. Cache the suite and the allowlist; the CI and the falsifier runs reuse them. Use a disposable canary string, never a real key; assert on every outbound channel. Spawn a sub-agent to run the isolated-harness CI so a loaded test skill cannot touch the real environment. Prove the suite with a planted-injection negative control - an all-green run with nothing to catch is theatre. Measure the falsifier (allowlist-only block rate) with the other layers genuinely disabled. Stop and ask the user only if there is no harness they own to test or no safe canary environment. Return a markdown report (threat model, file tree, suite-results-by-layer table, planted-injection catch evidence, canary-never-leaked proof, falsifier table) plus committed CI, suite, manifests and gate; print the commit hash. Keep every attack description abstract and defensive.

eval-gated-skill-evolution.mission: Build a two-way, eval-gated ratchet for your CLAUDE.md and skills: a held-out eval from your own history, an ablation sweep that deletes rules whose removal does not hurt, and a SkillOpt-style loop that merges only edits beating the benchmark - with a noise check that proves the eval is signal, not variance. Done means rules are both added and removed only on measured gains, winning traces are exported for a possible local fine-tune, and the ratchet is provably optimizing signal rather than noise.

deeper_not_bigger.professional_would: A practitioner who evolves agents properly does not 'append a lesson after every mistake' - that only ever grows the prompt into a tax. Following Microsoft SkillOpt (marc.kaz), they treat skill instructions as trainable parameters with an eval set and gate every rewrite on beating the benchmark, auto-rejecting edits that do not. Following Boris Cherny's simple mode (foundedceo) and cooper.simson's purge, they SUBTRACT: ablate each rule and delete what does not help, because stale rules make newer models dumber. They add a bilevel outer loop (raycfu) so the optimizer's own search strategy is revised, not just the skill text. They check noise first (the dive's falsifier). They lock risk/safety rules in code the loop cannot edit (raycfu's trading pattern), and they can export winning traces to a cheap local fine-tune (Soup).
deeper_not_bigger.rawest_material: Your exported Claude/ChatGPT chat history (the best personalization dataset, per angus.sewell's chat-history mining); your current CLAUDE.md and skills/ with their edit history; Microsoft SkillOpt (github.com/microsoft/SkillOpt) for the benchmark-gated self-rewrite loop; the SkillOpt/TextGrad baselines it reports beating; raycfu's bilevel-loop and hard-coded-risk-limits patterns; Prime Agent's self-modifying-scaffolding idea (wassimyounes_) with the caveat that a 0.1% margin is noise; Soup (martintrainhard) for small-model fine-tuning on winning traces.
deeper_not_bigger.methods_tools: A held-out eval: a cheap/local model (Haiku-class) tags ~40 representative tasks from your exported history with objective pass/fail criteria; an ablation harness that drops each CLAUDE.md rule and each skill one at a time and re-runs the eval; a SkillOpt-style optimizer loop (skills log their own failure notes; an optimizer proposes edits; only score-improving edits merge) on a nightly cron; a bilevel outer loop that edits the optimizer's strategy; a noise-floor check (variance of identical runs vs best-worst rule-set gap); safety/risk rules locked outside the editable set; optional Soup export of passing traces.
deeper_not_bigger.external_proof: A held-out eval (tasks not used to tune) where the ratcheted rule set beats the starting set, with the gain exceeding the run-to-run variance. The ablation sweep showing specific rules whose removal did not hurt (deleted) and whose removal did hurt (kept). The dive's falsifier answered: if variance between two identical runs exceeds the best-vs-worst rule-set gap, the eval is too noisy and the ratchet is optimizing noise - reported honestly. Optionally, a Soup fine-tune on winning traces matching the eval on a held-out slice.
deeper_not_bigger.rewritten_prompt: Act as an agent-optimization engineer. Build me a two-way, eval-gated ratchet for my CLAUDE.md and skills - one that DELETES as readily as it adds, and only on measured gains. Start by having a cheap/local model tag ~40 representative tasks from my exported chat history with objective pass/fail criteria; that is my held-out eval. Check noise first: run the same setup three times and measure variance - if variance rivals the gains I expect, tell me the eval is too noisy before I build anything on it. Then run an ablation sweep: drop each CLAUDE.md rule and each skill one at a time, re-run the eval, and delete anything whose removal does not hurt the score (stale rules for old models drag new ones down - cooper.simson, Cherny's simple mode). Then add a SkillOpt-style loop (github.com/microsoft/SkillOpt): skills log failure notes, an optimizer proposes edits, and only edits that beat the benchmark merge; put it on a nightly cron. Add a bilevel outer loop (raycfu) that revises the optimizer's strategy, not just the text. Lock my safety/risk rules outside the editable set. Export passing traces for a possible Soup fine-tune. Return the eval, the noise check, the ablation deletions and keeps, the gated edits, and a clear verdict on whether the ratchet beats baseline beyond noise.

eval-gated-skill-evolution.one_shot:
You are an agent-optimization engineer building a two-way, eval-gated ratchet for a CLAUDE.md and skills folder. Stance: subtract as readily as you add; nothing changes without a measured gain beyond noise; safety rules are never editable by the loop. No marketing language.

(2) a noise-floor check: variance of 2-3 identical runs vs the gains you expect; a go/no-go on trusting the eval. (4) a SkillOpt-style loop: skills log failure notes, an optimizer proposes edits, only benchmark-beating edits merge; on a nightly cron. (5) a bilevel outer loop revising the optimizer's strategy. Self-questions to answer in writing: Did I measure noise before trusting the eval (the falsifier)? Did the ratchet DELETE rules, or only add? Is any gain smaller than run-to-run variance? Are safety/risk rules genuinely uneditable by the loop? Did the optimizer merge an edit that did not beat the benchmark? Does the bilevel loop change strategy or just re-run the same instincts? Commit the eval, the ablation/optimizer harness, and the ratcheted CLAUDE.md/skills; print the hash.

steps.title: Build the held-out eval from history
steps.goal: Turn exported chat history into an objective eval with a cheap model.
steps.prompt: Establish the oracle. Export the chat history (angus.sewell's point: it is the best personalization dataset). Have a cheap or local model (Haiku-class) tag ~40 representative tasks from it, each with an objective pass/fail criterion a human could apply (not 'good' - e.g. 'produced valid JSON', 'followed the plan-first rule', 'refused unsafe action'). Make this a held-out set never used to tune rules. Build a runner that scores a given CLAUDE.md+skills setup against all ~40 tasks. This eval is what every ablation and every optimizer edit is judged against; a change that does not move it does not merge.
steps.expect: ~40 held-out tasks tagged with objective pass/fail criteria, plus a runner that scores a setup against them.
steps.audit: Check 5 criteria are objective enough for two graders to agree, and that the tasks span real usage (not just easy ones). Fail if criteria are subjective or the set is cherry-picked. On fail, re-tag with tighter criteria.

steps.title: Noise floor + falsifier
steps.goal: Prove the eval is signal before building the ratchet on it.
steps.prompt: Answer the dive's falsifier before anything else. Run the SAME setup against the eval 2-3 times and measure the variance between runs - this is the noise floor. Then estimate the gap you expect between the best and worst rule sets. If run-to-run variance is comparable to or larger than that best-vs-worst gap, STOP and report that the eval is too noisy and the whole ratchet would be optimizing noise; enlarge the eval or tighten criteria until variance is clearly below the gains you need to detect. Only proceed past this step if the noise floor is small enough to trust.
steps.expect: A measured run-to-run variance, a stated expected best-vs-worst gap, and a go/no-go verdict on the eval's trustworthiness.
steps.audit: Confirm the repeated runs used identical config. Fail if you proceed while variance rivals the expected gains. On fail, enlarge/tighten the eval before building the ratchet.

steps.title: Ablation sweep (the subtraction half)
steps.goal: Delete rules and skills whose removal does not hurt the eval.
steps.prompt: Run the subtraction half of the ratchet (cooper.simson's purge; Cherny's simple mode). Drop each CLAUDE.md rule and each skill ONE AT A TIME, re-run the eval, and record the score without it. Delete anything whose removal does not drop the score beyond the step-2 noise floor - EXCEPT safety/money/security rules, which are never deleted regardless of eval. Produce an ablation table: item, score with, score without, delta, deleted/kept/locked. The goal is the smallest rule set that holds the score; stale rules written for older models are the primary target.
steps.expect: An ablation table over every rule and skill, with deletions made for items whose removal did not hurt beyond noise, safety rules marked locked.
steps.audit: Confirm each deletion was decided by a real re-run and the delta is within noise. Confirm no safety/money rule was deleted. Fail if nothing was deleted (no real ablation) or a guardrail was cut. On fail, run the ablations properly and restore any guardrail.

steps.title: SkillOpt-style gated optimizer
steps.goal: Add edits only when they beat the benchmark; reject the rest.
steps.prompt: Build the addition half as a SkillOpt-style loop (github.com/microsoft/SkillOpt): (1) skills log their own failure notes as they run (angus.sewell's issues-table pattern). (2) An optimizer reads the notes and the eval failures and proposes an edit to a rule or skill. (3) The edit is applied to a copy, the eval is re-run, and the edit MERGES only if it beats the current benchmark beyond the noise floor; otherwise it is auto-rejected (SkillOpt's core behaviour). Isolate successful paths from failures. Put the loop on a nightly cron. Log every proposed edit with its before/after score and the merge/reject decision. Never let the optimizer touch the locked safety set.
steps.expect: A gated optimizer loop (log notes -> propose -> eval -> merge only if it beats baseline beyond noise) on a nightly cron, with an edit log and the safety set excluded.
steps.audit: Inspect the edit log: confirm every MERGED edit beat baseline beyond noise and every rejected one did not, and that no edit touched the locked set. Fail if a non-improving edit merged or a safety rule was edited. On fail, fix the gate threshold and the exclusion.

steps.title: Bilevel outer loop + lock safety
steps.goal: Revise the optimizer's strategy, and make risk rules uneditable.
steps.prompt: Add the two robustness pieces. (1) Bilevel outer loop (raycfu): wrap the SkillOpt loop with an outer loop that periodically revises the OPTIMIZER'S strategy - what kinds of edits it proposes - not just the skill text, so it does not keep trying the same few instincts (raycfu: single loops collapse onto a few favourite ideas). Measure whether the bilevel version explores more distinct edit types than the single loop. (2) Lock the safety set: move all safety/money/security/risk rules into a file or section the loop reads but cannot modify, enforced in code (raycfu's hard-coded-risk-limits pattern). Confirm the optimizer cannot write to it.
steps.expect: A bilevel outer loop shown to diversify edit types, and a code-enforced lock on the safety/risk rule set.
steps.audit: Compare edit-type diversity with and without the outer loop; confirm the optimizer physically cannot modify the locked file. Fail if the outer loop just re-runs the same edits or the safety file is writable by the loop. On fail, fix the strategy-revision step or the lock.

steps.title: Validate, export traces, gap report
steps.goal: Prove the ratchet beats baseline beyond noise; export winners; report honestly.
steps.prompt: Final validation. (1) Run the final ratcheted CLAUDE.md+skills against the held-out eval vs the starting set; report the gain and confirm it exceeds the step-2 noise floor. Apply wassimyounes_'s caveat: a sub-noise margin is NOT an improvement - say so if that is the case. (2) Export the passing traces (the task runs the winning rule set got right) in a format suitable for a Soup (martintrainhard) small-model fine-tune, and note whether a fine-tune is worthwhile. (3) Enumerate claims, mark verified/unverified/false, list missing pieces ranked by impact, fix the top two. Commit the eval, harness, and ratcheted setup; print the hash.
steps.expect: A final-vs-baseline eval comparison with a gain exceeding noise (or an honest null result), an exported passing-trace set for Soup, a claim ledger, and a committed setup with hash.
steps.audit: Confirm the final gain exceeds the noise floor; if not, state plainly the ratchet did not beat baseline. Confirm the exported traces are the passing ones, not all runs. Fail if a within-noise margin is reported as a win. On fail, report the null result honestly.

eval-gated-skill-evolution.gap_audit_prompt: Run after the ratchet is built. Enumerate every claim as a numbered list: the eval's objectivity and representativeness, the noise floor, each ablation deletion and keep, each merged/rejected optimizer edit, the bilevel loop's added diversity, the safety lock, and the final gain. Mark each VERIFIED (with run numbers), UNVERIFIED, or FALSE. Specifically re-check: were the eval criteria objective and the set truly held out; is the noise floor below the gains claimed (the falsifier); did the ablation actually DELETE rules, or only keep; did every merged edit beat baseline beyond noise and every rejected one fail; is any final gain within the noise band (a 0.1%-style non-result); is the safety/risk set genuinely uneditable by the loop; are the exported traces the passing ones. List missing pieces: subjective criteria, within-noise gains kept, no deletions, a writable safety file. Rank by impact on whether the ratchet is a real, safe improvement. Fix the top three and re-verify. Report what you could not fix and why. Do not report any improvement that is within the noise floor as a win.
self_questions: Did I measure the noise floor before trusting the eval (the falsifier), or build on sand?
Did the ratchet actually DELETE rules, or did it only add?
Is any reported gain smaller than the run-to-run variance?
Are the eval criteria objective enough for two graders to agree?
Is the held-out set truly held out, or did I tune rules on it?
Did the optimizer ever merge an edit that did not beat the benchmark?
Are safety, money and risk rules genuinely uneditable by the loop, enforced in code?
Does the bilevel outer loop change the optimizer's strategy, or re-run the same instincts?
Did I delete any stale rule written for an older model that drags the new one down?
Are the exported traces the passing ones, or did I export everything?
If the final margin is within noise, did I call it a null result rather than a win?
Did the ablation delta for each kept rule actually exceed the noise floor?
validation_oracles: On the held-out eval, the ratcheted rule set beats the starting set by more than the measured run-to-run variance (or the result is honestly reported as null).
The ablation table shows specific rules deleted because their removal did not hurt the eval, and kept rules each hurt when removed - proving two-way, not monotonic, change.
Every merged optimizer edit beat the benchmark beyond noise and every rejected edit did not, per the edit log (SkillOpt's gating behaviour).
The safety/money/risk rule set is provably uneditable by the loop (an attempted write is blocked in code).
The noise-floor check answers the falsifier: run-to-run variance is below the best-vs-worst rule-set gap, or the eval is declared too noisy to trust.
failure_modes: Monotonic ratchet: only adds, never deletes. Tell: CLAUDE.md keeps growing, no ablation deletions. Fix: run the ablation sweep and delete what removal does not hurt.
Optimizing noise: eval variance rivals the gains. Tell: results flip between identical runs. Fix: measure the noise floor first; enlarge/tighten the eval (the falsifier).
Ungated merges: edits applied without beating the benchmark. Tell: edit log has merges with no positive delta. Fix: enforce SkillOpt's merge-only-if-better gate beyond noise.
Editable safety rules: the loop rewrites risk limits. Tell: a guardrail changed after a run. Fix: lock safety/money rules in a code-enforced uneditable set.
Tuning on the held-out set: eval used to drive edits. Tell: great eval, worse real behaviour. Fix: keep a sealed set never used for tuning.
Collapsed bilevel loop: outer loop re-runs the same instincts. Tell: low edit-type diversity. Fix: make the outer loop revise the optimizer's strategy, measure diversity.
Sub-noise 'win': a 0.1%-style margin claimed as improvement (Prime Agent caveat). Tell: gain within variance. Fix: require the gain to exceed the noise floor; else report null.
eval-gated-skill-evolution.agent_direction: Reach first for the exported chat history and build the held-out eval, then measure the noise floor - the dive's falsifier gates everything, so do not build the ratchet until the eval is proven to carry signal. Cache the eval, the noise floor and the baseline score; ablations and optimizer edits all re-run against them. Run the subtraction half (ablation) and the addition half (SkillOpt-style gated optimizer) as separate, logged passes; spawn a sub-agent for the nightly optimizer loop so proposed edits are evaluated in isolation before merging. Never let any loop edit the safety/money/risk set - enforce that in code, not instruction. Apply the Prime Agent caveat: a sub-noise margin is not an improvement. Stop and ask the user only if there is no exported history to build an eval from. Return a markdown report (eval description, noise/falsifier verdict, ablation table, gated-edit log, locked safety set, 'Unverified and missing') plus the committed eval, harness and ratcheted CLAUDE.md/skills; print the commit hash, and export passing traces for a possible Soup fine-tune. If the ratchet does not beat baseline beyond noise, report that null result honestly.

plotter-loop.mission: Running this system produces a working geometry-to-ink pipeline: Go programs on Fogleman's ln that turn OBJ meshes, a Thomas attractor, a ray-marched Mandelbulb slice and a 3-lag phase-space embedding of BTC volatility into hidden-line SVGs, a vpype recipe that makes them plotter-ready, and a 6-print plotted series with photos, POD listings and one grant submission. Done means: every SVG plots on an A3 pen plotter without hand-picking paths, pen-up travel is measured before and after vpype, and the falsifier from the dive (line mush, originals not selling above POD price) has been tested rather than assumed away.

deeper_not_bigger.professional_would: A working plotter artist would treat line density as the real design variable: they would measure millimetres of ink per square centimetre per region, cap it so the paper does not buckle or the pen does not bleed through, and choose paths per surface (ln's 'texture is just the paths you choose') instead of drawing every triangle edge. They would make a test strip for each pen and paper combination before the series, plot a proof at A5, and version every plot by source hash, camera parameters and vpype command so an edition can be re-plotted identically.
deeper_not_bigger.rawest_material:
- fogleman/ln source at commit 12e6c6e (the Shape interface with Paths() and Intersect(), LoadOBJ, the csg, functions and skyscraper examples).
- abey79/vpype source and docs at commit e593ff0, especially linemerge, linesort, reloop, linesimplify, layout and stat.
- The DuckStation fork with the 3D-screenshot feature (its OBJ output folder) and one raw OBJ dump from a PS1 game you own.
- Mandelbulber2 source (buddhi1980/mandelbulber2) for the power-8 formula and the distance estimate d = 0.5*r*log(r)/dr.
- The Thomas attractor equations dx/dt = sin(y) - b*x (cyclic in x,y,z), b around 0.208186.
- A raw daily BTC-USD OHLC CSV covering one year, from which you compute realized volatility yourself.
- axicli or GRBL docs for your machine.
deeper_not_bigger.methods_tools: Go 1.22+ with ln; a custom ln Shape that uses the full mesh for Intersect() (occlusion) but returns only feature edges (dihedral angle above a threshold, plus silhouette edges) from Paths(); Python with trimesh for mesh cleanup, decimation and feature-edge extraction; headless Blender for cleanup; scipy solve_ivp; pandas for the delay embedding; vpype pipeline 'read in.svg linemerge --tolerance 0.1mm linesort reloop linesimplify --tolerance 0.05mm layout -m 15mm a3 stat write out.svg'; axicli or vpype-gcode for output.
deeper_not_bigger.external_proof: The plotter itself is the oracle: a plot that finishes without pen skips, paper tear or hand-edited paths. vpype stat gives the pen-up length before and after, which tests the creator's 86% reduction claim on your files. A stranger shown the 6 plots without captions should be able to say what at least half of the subjects are (readability). A sale of an original above the POD reproduction price, and the grant's accept/reject email, are the market oracles.
deeper_not_bigger.rewritten_prompt: You are building a pen-plotter pipeline on Michael Fogleman's ln (Go) and abey79's vpype. Do not just render OBJs; make them readable in ink. Build: (1) an ln Shape type that occludes with the full mesh but draws only feature and silhouette edges chosen by a dihedral-angle threshold, so DuckStation PS1 rips and Orbiter or LiDAR phone scans do not turn into triangle mush; (2) emitters for a Thomas attractor (b=0.208186) and a 3-lag (tau=3) delay embedding of one year of BTC-USD daily realized volatility, each as 3D polylines rendered through ln; (3) one Mandelbulb slice stack using the distance estimate from Mandelbulber2. Every SVG must go through a pinned vpype command, and you must report vpype stat pen-up length before and after for each file, so the claimed 86% pen-up reduction is measured, not repeated. Compute ink density in mm per cm2 per 1 cm grid cell and flag cells above a cap I set. Log source file hash, camera eye/center/up, fovy, ln step and the vpype command per plot into a manifest. Produce a 6-print A3 series with an A5 proof of each. Finish with a gap report: which subjects were unreadable, which needed hand edits (that is a failure), and whether the falsifier fired.

plotter-loop.one_shot:
ROLE AND STANCE
You are a plotter artist and graphics engineer. You treat the pen plotter as the final judge and every claim from the source posts as a hypothesis to measure. You do not hand-pick paths; if a source needs hand-picking, you report it as a failure of the pipeline.

CONTEXT
- ln by Michael Fogleman (github.com/fogleman/ln, commit 12e6c6e): Go library that renders 3D scenes to 2D vector paths by ray-testing each chopped path segment toward the camera. Texture is the set of paths you put on a surface. Supports CSG, function surfaces, OBJ meshes.
- vpype by abey79 (commit e593ff0): linemerge + linesort reportedly cut pen-up travel 86% (105,271 to a much smaller number) in the creator's example.
- Sources to feed it: a DuckStation 3D-screenshot OBJ rip of a PS1 scene (lands in the screenshot 3D folder, scene placement intact), a smartphone scan (Orbiter rig) or Raspberry Pi LiDAR point cloud meshed to OBJ, a Mandelbulb (power 8, distance estimate d = 0.5*r*log(r)/dr, reference Mandelbulber2), a Thomas cyclically symmetric attractor, a 3-lag phase-space embedding of BTC-USD volatility (quant.dhawan used tau=3), and optionally a Blender scene generated by a Python script and a curlicue or harmonograph curve.
- Sales: Printful, Gelato, Fine Art America POD; Artist Grant ($1,200, $30 fee, 3-5 images).

HARD CONSTRAINTS
- All geometry goes through ln for hidden-line removal; no raster tracing.
- Every SVG passes through one pinned vpype command; record it.
- No manual path deletion. If a file is unreadable, change the path generator, not the SVG.
- Ink density cap: flag any 1 cm grid cell above 60 mm of line per cm2 (adjust after the pen test strip, then keep fixed).
- The BTC piece is a drawing of data, not a trading signal; make no predictive claims in titles or listings.
- Rip only from games the user owns; flag trademarked characters before selling.

DELIVERABLES, IN ORDER
1. ground_truth.md: ln and vpype versions built from source, an example from ln's repo rendered to SVG, and vpype stat for it before and after the pipeline.
2. featureshape.go: an ln Shape that uses the full triangle mesh for Intersect() and returns only feature edges (dihedral angle above a threshold, default 30 degrees) plus silhouette edges for Paths(). Include a test that renders ln's unit cube and returns exactly 12 visible-or-hidden candidate edges.
3. sources/: Go or Python emitters for the PS1 rip, one scan, the Thomas attractor (solve_ivp, b=0.208186, 200k steps, drop first 5%), the Mandelbulb as stacked horizontal slices, and the BTC embedding (log returns, 20-day realized vol, points (v_t, v_t-3, v_t-6), one polyline per month).
4. render.sh: one command per piece producing raw.svg, plot.svg, a PNG preview, and a manifest.json row (source hash, eye, center, up, fovy, near, far, ln step, vpype command, pen-up before/after, total line length, max density cell).
5. series/: 6 A3 SVGs titled by subject and date range, plus A5 proofs.
6. plot_log.md: per plot, pen, paper, duration, failures.
7. listing_kit/: photo checklist, edition policy, pricing table, grant email draft.

BUILT-IN GAP ANALYSIS
Keep a running GAPS section in ground_truth.md. For every claim you rely on, mark VERIFIED (with the command and output), UNVERIFIED, or FALSE. At minimum: the 86% pen-up reduction on your files; DuckStation rips keeping scene placement; feature-edge filtering making rips readable; the BTC embedding versus a shuffled-returns control. Fill every gap you can by running the check; list the rest with what would close them.

SELF-QUESTIONS BEFORE FINISHING
- Does any plot still need a human to delete paths?
- Did I render the shuffled-volatility control, and can a viewer tell it apart from the real embedding?
- Is line density under the cap everywhere, or will the pen soak the paper?
- Is the original priced above the POD print?

STOP CONDITIONS
Stop and report if ln cannot load the OBJ after Blender cleanup, if any source exceeds 2 hours estimated plot time at A3, or if the plotter is not available (deliver SVGs and previews, mark plot steps UNVERIFIED).

RETURN FORMAT
A short summary, then the manifest.json table, the GAPS list with statuses, the falsifier verdict (fired / did not fire / not yet testable) and the file tree.

steps.title: Ground truth: build ln and vpype from source
steps.goal: Prove the toolchain works and measure the pen-up claim on a known example.
steps.prompt: Clone github.com/fogleman/ln at commit 12e6c6e7445909f817f1b8d5581be4255ffa1437 and github.com/abey79/vpype at e593ff0c2b13e48be2b3aa10e1c8d71c1b21dc0. Build ln with Go 1.22+ and install vpype in a fresh venv with pip install -e. Run ln's cube and skyscrapers examples to SVG. For each SVG run 'vpype read raw.svg stat' and then 'vpype read raw.svg linemerge --tolerance 0.1mm linesort reloop linesimplify --tolerance 0.05mm stat write plot.svg'. Record total length, pen-up length and path count before and after. The creator claimed an 86% pen-up reduction (105,271 down) on ln's examples with added camera motion; compute your own percentage on both examples. Read ln's Shape interface (Compile, BoundingBox, Contains, Intersect, Paths) and write two sentences on how hidden-line removal works (segments chopped, each point ray-tested toward the eye). Write ground_truth.md with versions, commands, the numbers table and a GAPS section.
steps.expect: ground_truth.md with exact versions, two before/after stat tables, a computed pen-up reduction percentage per example, and a GAPS list.
steps.audit: Re-run the vpype pipeline once and confirm the stat numbers are identical (determinism). If pen-up reduction differs from 86% by more than 20 points, mark the claim UNVERIFIED for your setup and note why (different scene, tolerance). Fail if any command was paraphrased rather than copied.

steps.title: Feature-edge shape for meshes
steps.goal: Make ripped and scanned meshes readable without hand-picking paths.
steps.prompt: Using ground_truth.md, write featureshape.go: a type FeatureMesh wrapping ln.Mesh. Intersect() and BoundingBox() delegate to the full mesh so occlusion stays exact. Paths() returns only (a) edges whose adjacent triangle normals differ by more than a configurable dihedral angle (default 30 degrees), (b) boundary edges, and optionally (c) parallel slice lines (ln.Paths from plane cuts every N mm) as hatching on large flat faces. Build an edge map keyed by sorted vertex index pairs; weld duplicate vertices first with a 1e-5 tolerance because PS1 rips and scans are unwelded. Add a Go test: a unit cube yields 12 feature edges; a 1,000-triangle sphere at 30 degrees yields 0 feature edges and you must fall back to silhouette or slice paths. Render one DuckStation rip OBJ both ways (all triangle edges vs FeatureMesh) and report path counts and total length for each.
steps.expect: featureshape.go, a passing go test, and two SVGs of the same rip with a path-count comparison (expect a 5-20x reduction).
steps.audit: Open both SVGs as PNG previews side by side. Fail if the FeatureMesh version loses the object's outline or if path count did not drop by at least 3x. On fail, inspect welding (count unique vertices before and after) before changing the angle.

steps.title: Mesh sources: PS1 rip and phone or LiDAR scan
steps.goal: Turn real captured geometry into clean OBJs ln can load.
steps.prompt: Take one OBJ from the DuckStation 3D-screenshot folder (a game the user owns) and one scan (Orbiter photogrammetry or the Raspberry Pi LiDAR cloud meshed with Open3D Poisson reconstruction). Write clean_mesh.py that runs Blender headless (blender -b -P clean_mesh.py -- in.obj out.obj): merge by distance 0.0001, delete loose, recalculate normals outside, decimate to at most 40k triangles, apply transforms, export OBJ with triangulated faces. Verify the rip kept scene placement as the creator said (check that multiple objects keep their relative offsets). Render each through FeatureMesh with three camera positions; choose the one with the most readable silhouette and the lowest max ink-density cell. Write the chosen eye, center, up, fovy, the dihedral angle used and the triangle counts before and after cleanup into manifest.json.
steps.expect: Two cleaned OBJs under 40k triangles, three preview PNGs each, and manifest rows.
steps.audit: Confirm ln loads each OBJ without panics and the render completes under 10 minutes. Compute density per 1 cm cell; fail if any cell exceeds the cap. On fail, raise the dihedral angle or switch large faces to slice hatching, then re-render.

steps.title: Math sources: attractor, Mandelbulb, BTC embedding
steps.goal: Emit mathematical geometry as 3D polylines for ln.
steps.prompt: Write three emitters that output polylines as JSON arrays of [x,y,z] for a small Go loader that wraps them in ln.NewPath and renders with a mesh or no occluder. (1) Thomas attractor: dx/dt = sin(y) - b*x, dy/dt = sin(z) - b*y, dz/dt = sin(x) - b*z, b = 0.208186, scipy solve_ivp RK45, 200,000 samples, drop the first 5%, split into polylines every 2,000 points. (2) Mandelbulb: power 8 in spherical coordinates (r to r^8, theta and phi times 8, add c), ray-march with the distance estimate 0.5*r*log(r)/dr ported from Mandelbulber2, extract 60 horizontal contour slices with marching squares (skimage.measure.find_contours) and draw them as stacked rings; occlude with a coarse marching-cubes mesh. (3) BTC: daily BTC-USD closes for one year, log returns, 20-day rolling std, embed (v_t, v_t-3, v_t-6), one polyline per calendar month. Also emit a control: the same pipeline on shuffled returns.
steps.expect: Three emitters, four SVGs (including the shuffled control) and manifest rows.
steps.audit: Check the attractor stays bounded (all coordinates within about |5|) and is not a fixed point. Show the real and shuffled BTC plots to yourself unlabeled; if you cannot tell which is which, title the piece honestly and drop any 'regime' language.

steps.title: Plot-ready series and plotting
steps.goal: Produce 6 A3 prints with pinned vpype settings and plot them.
steps.prompt: Select 6 pieces from steps 3-4 (at least one mesh, one attractor, the BTC embedding). For each, write a render.sh entry that produces raw.svg and plot.svg via 'vpype read raw.svg linemerge --tolerance 0.1mm linesort reloop linesimplify --tolerance 0.05mm layout -m 15mm a3 stat write plot.svg'. If you use two pen weights, split into layers by path length or depth (near paths on layer 1 with the thicker pen) and use vpype's layer flags. Estimate plot time from total length at your plotter's speed; reject any piece over 2 hours. Plot an A5 proof of each first (layout a5), then the A3 original. For AxiDraw use axicli with a pinned config; for a DIY GRBL machine use vpype-gcode with a named profile. Log pen, paper, duration and every failure in plot_log.md.
steps.expect: 6 plot.svg files, 6 A5 proofs, 6 A3 originals, plot_log.md, manifest with pen-up before/after per piece.
steps.audit: Fail any plot that needed a pause to fix the machine more than once, tore paper, or bled through. Fix the cause (density, speed, pen pressure) in the generator and re-plot; never edit the SVG by hand.

steps.title: Photograph, list, apply
steps.goal: Turn the series into products and one grant submission.
steps.prompt: Photograph each A3 original flat in overcast window daylight, no flash, camera square to the paper (check with a level), include a gray card in a reference frame, crop to the paper edge. Export 300 dpi files at A3 for POD. Write listing_kit/: an edition policy (each original is 1/1, signed and dated, with the manifest hash on the back; POD reproductions are open editions), a pricing table pulling base cost from Printful and Gelato product pages for A3 matte prints, and Fine Art America markups. Price the original at least 3x the highest POD retail price. Create at least 10 listings as the creator advised (the 6 plots plus 4 proofs or details). Draft the Artist Grant email: website link or 3-5 images, short bio, social-sharing permission, $30 fee, check the next of the three yearly deadlines.
steps.expect: Photo set, listing_kit with pricing math, 10 listings drafted, grant email draft.
steps.audit: Check every price covers base cost plus platform fee plus shipping. Fail if any photo shows glare or keystone (paper edges not parallel). Do not submit or publish anything; leave final submission to the user.

steps.title: Validate against oracles and write the gap report
steps.goal: Decide whether the loop is a practice or a toy.
steps.prompt: Read manifest.json, plot_log.md, ground_truth.md and listing_kit. Score the falsifier from the dive: (a) did any mesh need hand-picked paths? (b) did any original sell above the POD print price within the listing window? Mark each VERIFIED, FALSE or NOT YET TESTABLE. Run the oracles: re-plot one piece from its manifest and compare the two physical plots and the two SVG hashes; show the 6 plots uncaptioned to three people and record how many subjects each identifies; recompute pen-up reduction across all 6 and report mean and range versus the claimed 86%. Write gap_report.md: claims table with evidence, unresolved gaps ranked by impact on the falsifier, and the three changes that would most improve readability or sales, each with the file it touches.
steps.expect: gap_report.md with a claims table, oracle results, falsifier verdict and ranked next fixes.
steps.audit: Every VERIFIED row must cite a file and line or a command output. Fail the report if any row says verified without evidence; downgrade it to UNVERIFIED.

plotter-loop.gap_audit_prompt: You are auditing a finished ln + vpype pen-plotter series. Inputs: manifest.json, plot_log.md, ground_truth.md, featureshape.go, the six plot.svg files, listing_kit/. Do not trust the builder's summary. 1) Enumerate every claim the build makes: pen-up reductions per file, triangle counts, density caps met, re-plot determinism, readability, that DuckStation rips keep scene placement, that the BTC embedding differs from its shuffled control, pricing margins. 2) For each, re-run the check (vpype stat on plot.svg, go test, density script, hash comparison) and mark VERIFIED, UNVERIFIED or FALSE with the output. 3) Look for silent cheating: SVGs edited after vpype (compare file mtimes and hashes against manifest), paths deleted by hand, a control that was never rendered, prices that omit shipping. 4) List missing pieces: e.g. no A5 proof for a piece, no pen test strip, no license check on game content. 5) Rank gaps by how much they affect the falsifier (readability without hand-picking; originals selling above POD). 6) Fix the top three now and re-run their checks. 7) Report what you could not fix and why (no plotter access, no sales yet), with the exact next action for each.
self_questions: Did any mesh source still need a human to delete paths, which the dive says makes the loop a toy?
Did I weld vertices before computing feature edges, or are PS1 rip seams producing fake edges?
Is the 86% pen-up claim measured on my files, and with which linemerge tolerance?
Does the shuffled-returns BTC control look different from the real embedding, or is the 'hidden dynamics' story decoration?
Does the Mandelbulb slice stack read as a solid, or does it need occlusion I skipped?

overfit-proof-autoresearch.mission: Running this system builds a strategy autoresearch loop whose judge is designed to reject overfitting: Claude proposes strategy edits to a VectorBT backtester, every proposal is logged to a trials table, and a four-part gate (net of realistic fees, beats 95% of a permutation null, positive deflated Sharpe using the logged trial count, one-shot held-out year) decides survival. It is for a solo builder who wants to know cheaply whether they have any edge. Done means the judge rejects every strategy on pure-noise synthetic prices, survivors pass a second-model look-ahead audit, and any survivor runs only on paper with caps until the paper oracle passes. No real money, and no return is promised.

They would treat every proposal, including the ones the agent discarded, as a trial for deflation, and compute the probability of backtest overfitting with combinatorially symmetric cross-validation rather than a single train/test split. They would require survival at 2x modeled per-venue costs. They would lock the held-out year physically (hash-committed, read by a separate process) so the loop cannot peek, and put risk limits in a process the agent cannot edit.

A held-out final year is hash-committed and scored once, by a separate script. Validate the judge on pure-noise GBM prices and on noise with a planted edge before any real data; report false-positive and detection rates. overfit-proof-autoresearch.one_shot:
ROLE AND STANCE
You are a quantitative researcher whose job is to stop yourself from fooling yourself. The deliverable is a judge that cannot be gamed by an automated search, then a loop that uses it. 'No survivors' is a valid and likely result. You never promise returns, and you never touch real money.

CONTEXT
- Microsoft SkillOpt (github.com/microsoft/SkillOpt): an optimizer rewrites instructions from results and auto-rejects edits that do not beat a benchmark. Pointed at a backtest, that is an overfitting machine.
- Karpathy-style autoresearch (try, test, keep or revert) and raycfu's bilevel loop (an outer coach rewrites the inner search playbook; claimed about 5x better on Karpathy's benchmark).
- raycfu's critic-agent trading loop (rewrites losing rules; hard-coded stop-loss outside the agent; failure database).
- quant.dhawan: 25,000 Monte Carlo shuffles of BTC daily returns; Wasserstein and Sinkhorn drift between backtest and live.
- @heidioftheeast's list: probability of backtest overfitting, Sharpe statistics.
- avi_mukesh: hourly crypto dollar-neutral reversal, Sharpe over 5 before costs, gone after fees.
- Claudex (nateherkai): one model never grades its own work. Munger inversion: list how the loop fools you, block each path.

HARD CONSTRAINTS
- No real orders. Paper account or exchange testnet only. Position cap 2% of paper equity per name, gross exposure cap 100%, daily loss stop 1%, drawdown kill 10%. These live in risk_guard.py, run as a separate process with read-only access for the agent.
- Every proposal, including crashes and agent-discarded ideas, is a row in trials.sqlite (id, timestamp, parent id, code hash, params JSON, in-sample metrics, judge verdict, reason).
- The held-out year (the most recent 12 months) is never loaded by the loop. holdout_score.py checks a SHA-256 commitment file and refuses to run twice for the same strategy hash.
- Costs: per-venue taker fee from the published schedule, half-spread from data, slippage 5 bps per side minimum; survivors must stay positive at 2x costs.

DELIVERABLES, IN ORDER
1. data/: Binance hourly OHLCV for BTC, ETH, SOL and 5 more liquid pairs, 4+ years, with a data_quality.md (gaps, duplicates, timezone).
2. judge.py with four tests: net-of-cost Sharpe; permutation p-value (2,000 draws, permute signal positions against returns and also stationary block bootstrap); deflated Sharpe ratio using N from trials.sqlite and the variance of trial Sharpes; PBO via CSCV with 16 blocks.
3. judge_validation.md: run the judge on 200 pure-noise GBM datasets (false-positive rate must be at most 5%) and on 200 datasets with a planted signal of known Sharpe 1.5 (report detection rate). Also on avi_mukesh's reversal, which must fail on costs.
4. loop.py: Claude proposes edits as diffs to strategies/; each is backtested in VectorBT, logged, judged. A coach step every 50 trials reads the trials table and rewrites search_playbook.md, and a failure-memory query blocks near-duplicate ideas.
5. audit/: for each survivor, a second model (Codex or GPT) reviews the code for look-ahead bias using a checklist; findings logged.
6. paper/: survivors run on paper with a control arm (buy-and-hold and random entries with matched turnover), daily Wasserstein distance between backtest and live return distributions, auto-retire on breach.
7. report.md.

BUILT-IN GAP ANALYSIS
Maintain GAPS in report.md. Mark each claim VERIFIED, UNVERIFIED or FALSE with evidence: judge false-positive rate on noise; that N in the deflated Sharpe equals the trials row count; that the holdout was never read (grep the loop's file access log); that costs match current fee schedules; that bilevel coaching changed idea diversity (count distinct strategy families per 50 trials before and after); that the 25,000-shuffle method in the source post tests edge at all. Fill what you can by running it.

SELF-QUESTIONS
- If I feed the loop pure noise for 500 trials, does anything pass?
- Is N counting every attempt, or only the ones that compiled?
- Did the permutation null preserve volatility clustering, or is it too easy to beat?
- Could any feature use data from bar t+1?

STOP CONDITIONS
Stop when the noise falsifier fails (fix the judge first), when 1,000 trials produce no survivors (report it), or when a survivor reaches paper. Ask before any step that would touch a live account.

RETURN FORMAT
report.md with: judge validation table, trials count, survivors with all four gate scores, audit findings, paper status, GAPS, and an explicit line: 'No real money until the paper oracle passes.'

steps.title: Ground truth: data, costs, source methods
steps.goal: Assemble raw data, real fee schedules and the original papers before writing any loop.
steps.prompt: Download hourly OHLCV for BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT, SOLUSDT and 5 other liquid USDT pairs from data.binance.vision for at least 4 years. Check gaps, duplicate timestamps, UTC alignment and zero-volume bars; write data_quality.md. Record current spot and perp taker fees from the exchange's fee page and estimate half-spread from the data or a book snapshot. Read Bailey et al. 2015 (PBO via CSCV) and Bailey and Lopez de Prado 2014 (deflated Sharpe ratio) and write the exact formulas you will implement, with variable definitions. Read the SkillOpt repo and note precisely where it accepts or rejects an edit. Write a note on quant.dhawan's 25,000-shuffle test: shuffling a strategy's daily returns keeps their mean and Sharpe unchanged, so it only tests drawdown path; state what null you will use instead. Commit a SHA-256 hash of the last 12 months of data to holdout.commit and move those rows to a directory the loop cannot read.
steps.expect: data/ with a quality report, fees.json, formulas.md with PBO and DSR math, a SkillOpt note, holdout.commit.
steps.audit: Recompute the holdout hash and confirm it matches. Fail if any formula lacks a citation or if the loop's data path includes the holdout dates. Fix before step 2.

steps.title: Build the judge
steps.goal: Implement the four-part gate as tested code.
steps.prompt: Write judge.py exposing judge(strategy_returns, positions, prices, trials_db) returning a dict with four sub-verdicts and a final pass flag. (1) Costs: apply taker fee from fees.json, half-spread and 5 bps slippage per side to every position change; compute net annualized Sharpe; recompute at 2x costs; both must be positive. (2) Permutation: 2,000 draws permuting the position series in blocks of 24 hours against fixed returns, plus a stationary block bootstrap of returns; pass if net Sharpe exceeds the 95th percentile of both. (3) Deflated Sharpe: N = SELECT COUNT(*) FROM trials (all rows), variance of trial Sharpes from the same table, skew and kurtosis of the candidate's returns; pass if DSR probability exceeds 0.95. (4) PBO: CSCV with 16 equal blocks over the in-sample period across the candidate's parameter neighbourhood; pass if PBO under 0.2. Write pytest tests for each with tiny fixtures.
steps.expect: judge.py with four functions, pytest passing, a docstring citing each paper.
steps.audit: Test that a strategy with zero turnover pays zero costs, that N changes when a row is inserted, and that permutation p-values are uniform on random positions (KS test p over 0.05). Fail and fix on any mismatch.

steps.title: Validate the judge on noise and planted signals
steps.goal: Measure the judge's false-positive and detection rates before showing it a market.
steps.prompt: Generate 200 pure-noise datasets: GBM hourly prices for 8 assets with volatility and correlation matched to the real data, plus 200 datasets where the real returns are shuffled within assets. Generate 200 planted-signal datasets where a known feature predicts the next hour with an implied gross Sharpe of 1.5 after costs. For each dataset, run a mini-search of 100 random parameter variants of three families (momentum, reversal, breakout), logging each to a temporary trials table, and judge the best. Report: false-positive rate on noise (must be at most 5%; target under 1%), detection rate on planted signal, and which gate did the rejecting. Also run avi_mukesh's hourly dollar-neutral reversal on real data; it must fail the cost gate. Write judge_validation.md.
steps.expect: judge_validation.md with a table: dataset type, n, pass rate, failing gate counts.
steps.audit: If anything passes on noise above 5%, stop: inspect which gate let it through, tighten it, rerun all 600 datasets. Never proceed to step 4 with a failing falsifier.

steps.title: The autoresearch loop with bilevel coach
steps.goal: Let Claude search strategy space under the validated judge.
steps.prompt: Write loop.py. Each iteration: Claude reads search_playbook.md, the last 30 trials and the failure-memory list, then proposes one change as a unified diff to a file in strategies/ (signals only; it cannot edit judge.py, costs, risk_guard.py or data paths; enforce with file permissions and a diff path allowlist). Apply, backtest in VectorBT on in-sample data only, insert a trials row before judging (so crashes count), judge, record verdict and reason. Every 50 trials a coach call reads the trials table, counts distinct strategy families and repeated ideas, and rewrites search_playbook.md to push exploration away from the overused families (the bilevel idea). Embed rejected ideas and block proposals with cosine similarity over 0.9 to a rejected one. Run 500 trials. Log total tokens and wall time.
steps.expect: trials.sqlite with 500+ rows, search_playbook.md history, a diversity chart of families per 50 trials, a list of survivors (possibly empty).
steps.audit: Confirm row count equals iterations attempted, that no diff touched a protected path, and that the coach changed family diversity. If survivors exist, check whether they share one family with tweaked parameters; if so, treat them as one trial family and recheck PBO.

steps.title: Cross-model look-ahead audit and holdout
steps.goal: Have a different model audit survivors, then score the holdout once.
steps.prompt: For each survivor, send the strategy code and the backtest harness to a second model (Codex or GPT, not Claude) with this checklist: any shift with a negative lag, rolling or expanding windows that include the current bar's close when trading at that close, normalization fitted on the full sample, use of future-listed assets (survivorship), fills at prices the strategy could not have seen, and timezone misalignment. Require line-cited findings. Fix confirmed issues, re-judge, and log the re-judge as new trials. Then, for survivors still passing, run holdout_score.py once per strategy hash; it verifies holdout.commit, loads the sealed year, computes net Sharpe at 1x and 2x costs, and writes the result to an append-only file. A survivor must be net positive on the holdout at 2x costs.
steps.expect: audit/ with per-survivor findings, re-judged trials rows, holdout_results.jsonl with one line per strategy.
steps.audit: Confirm holdout_score.py refused a second run for the same hash (test it). Fail the step if any survivor reached holdout without a second-model audit.

steps.title: Paper trading with a control and drift kill
steps.goal: Test survivors forward on paper only, against a control.
steps.prompt: Deploy survivors to a paper account (Alpaca paper or an exchange testnet) with risk_guard.py running as a separate process: 2% of paper equity per position, 100% gross cap, 1% daily loss stop, 10% drawdown kill, and it alone holds the API key. Run a control arm in parallel: buy-and-hold of the same universe and a random-entry strategy with matched turnover and costs. Each day compute the Wasserstein distance (scipy.stats.wasserstein_distance) and Sinkhorn divergence (ot.sinkhorn2) between the backtest return distribution and the trailing 20-day live distribution; retire the strategy automatically if the distance exceeds the 99th percentile of the same statistic computed on rolling in-sample windows. Track slippage of paper fills versus modeled fills per order. Run at least 60 trading days before any verdict.
steps.expect: paper/ with daily logs, control comparisons, drift series, fills versus model, and retirement events.
steps.audit: Check that risk_guard.py actually blocked an oversized test order (send one deliberately on paper). Fail if the agent process holds any exchange key. No real money at this step under any result.

steps.title: Validate against oracles and write the gap report
steps.goal: Decide honestly whether anything has an edge.
steps.prompt: Read judge_validation.md, trials.sqlite, audit/, holdout_results.jsonl and paper/. Produce report.md with: judge false-positive and detection rates; total trials N and how many survived each gate; survivors' net Sharpe, DSR, PBO and holdout score; second-model findings; paper results versus the control arm with confidence intervals (block bootstrap); drift events. State the verdict as one of: no edge found; edge survived backtest but not paper; edge survived paper versus control for 60+ days. Only the last permits discussing real money, and even then write: 'No real money until the user reviews this report and the paper oracle has passed; start at the minimum size with the same caps.' Then write GAPS: each claim marked VERIFIED, UNVERIFIED or FALSE with evidence, and the three highest-impact gaps fixed or with a stated reason.
steps.expect: report.md with verdict, tables, GAPS and the no-real-money line.
steps.audit: Cross-check every number in report.md against its source file. Fail if the verdict is stronger than the evidence (for example, 'edge' with fewer than 60 paper days).

overfit-proof-autoresearch.gap_audit_prompt: You are an independent auditor of a strategy autoresearch build. Assume it is overfit until shown otherwise. Inputs: judge.py, judge_validation.md, trials.sqlite, loop.py, audit/, holdout_results.jsonl, paper/, report.md. 1) List every claim: false-positive rate, N used in deflation, PBO values, holdout never read, costs current, risk caps enforced, paper beats control. 2) Re-verify each: run the judge's noise test on 50 fresh noise datasets; compare N in the DSR call to SELECT COUNT(*) FROM trials; grep the loop's file access log and source for holdout paths; diff fees.json against the exchange page; send an oversized order on paper and confirm risk_guard blocks it; recompute paper versus control with a block bootstrap. Mark each VERIFIED, UNVERIFIED or FALSE with output. 3) Hunt bypasses: trials deleted or never logged, strategies that import from judge or data modules, survivors that are parameter clones of each other, look-ahead the second model missed (check every shift and rolling call yourself). 4) Rank gaps by risk of a false 'edge' verdict. 5) Fix the top three now and rerun their checks. 6) Report what you could not fix and why. Never upgrade the verdict; you may only downgrade it.
self_questions: If I seed the loop with pure-noise prices, does anything pass the judge?
Is N in the deflated Sharpe the count of every trials row, including crashes and coach-discarded ideas?
Does my permutation null preserve volatility clustering, or does it make any trend-follower look significant?
Did the source post's 25,000 return shuffles test edge at all, given that shuffling keeps the mean?
Is any survivor using a bar's close to trade at that same close?
Are survivors distinct ideas or one idea with neighbouring parameters?
Do survivors stay positive at 2x costs and with one bar of execution delay?
Could the agent edit risk limits, fee assumptions or the holdout path through any route?
Is the paper result better than the matched-turnover random control with a confidence interval excluding zero?
Have I written that no real money moves until the paper oracle passes?
validation_oracles: Pure-noise falsifier: 200 GBM and 200 shuffled-return datasets run through the full search; the judge passes at most 5% (target under 1%), recorded in judge_validation.md.
Planted-signal detection: datasets with a known after-cost Sharpe of 1.5; the judge detects it in a reported share of runs.
Sealed holdout: holdout_score.py verifies the SHA-256 commitment and scores each strategy hash once; second attempts are refused.
Cross-provider audit: Codex or GPT reviews each survivor for look-ahead with line-cited findings.

Paper oracle: at least 60 trading days on a paper account or testnet versus buy-and-hold and matched-turnover random controls, with Wasserstein drift under the preset threshold and risk_guard blocking a deliberate oversized order.
failure_modes: Judge gamed by search volume. Tell: survivors appear only after hundreds of trials and DSR used a small N. Fix: N from the full trials table, rerun the noise falsifier.
Fees ignored or underestimated. Tell: high-turnover survivors like the hourly reversal with a gross Sharpe over 5. Fix: per-venue taker fees, spread, slippage and a 2x-cost survival test.
Look-ahead leak. Tell: holdout or paper collapses relative to in-sample, or Sharpe implausibly high. Fix: second-model audit plus your own grep for negative shifts and centered windows.
Holdout contamination. Tell: the loop's code or logs reference holdout dates. Fix: sealed directory, hash commitment, separate scoring process.
Agent edits its guardrails. Tell: diffs touching judge.py or risk_guard.py. Fix: path allowlist.
Paper luck read as edge. Tell: 20 good days declared a win. Fix: 60+ days, bootstrap interval versus the control, no real money until it passes.
overfit-proof-autoresearch.agent_direction: Run steps strictly in order; step 3 is a hard gate and nothing proceeds while noise passes the judge. Reach first for Python, vectorbt, SQLite and pytest; cache downloaded Binance files and backtest results keyed by strategy code hash plus data range. Delegate data download and the PBO/DSR code to sub-agents; review both against the papers. The second-model audit must use a different provider (Codex or GPT); do not let Claude grade Claude. Never place a real order, never request or print exchange secrets, and keep API keys only in risk_guard.py's environment loaded at runtime. Stop and ask the user before connecting any paper or testnet account and before any discussion of live capital. Return: judge.py and tests, judge_validation.md, trials.sqlite, loop.py, search_playbook.md history, audit/, holdout_results.jsonl, paper/, report.md with the verdict and the line 'No real money until the paper oracle passes.'

ambient-executive-function.mission: Running this system builds a small always-on desk object, an ESP32 driving a 2.7 inch Sharp memory LCD in a printed stand, that shows the top three lines of NOW.md and the count of Claude Code sessions waiting for approval, plus NFC tags that log done/started/leaving with one tap through an iOS Shortcut. It is for someone whose executive-function failure is the remembering-to-look step. Done means the display updates within 10 seconds of a hook or tap, a 14-day study with a baseline and a phone-notification comparison has run, and the dive's falsifier (habituation by week two, no drop in agent wait time) has been scored from logs.

deeper_not_bigger.professional_would: A human-factors researcher would design the 14 days as an ABAB single-case study, not a before/after: baseline logging with the display off, display on, phone notifications instead, display on again. ROLE AND STANCE
You are an embedded engineer and human-factors researcher building an ambient-display intervention for executive-function friction. You build the smallest device that works, then let the logs decide whether it helps. You expect novelty and the Hawthorne effect to inflate early results and you design for that.

CONTEXT
- Problem framing: OpenAI's $230 Codex Micro controller; cooper.simson's MacBook notch app showing working / needs attention / done; jarrenrocks' Bot Crossing where 80 agents raise their hands; the.poet.engineer's gesture concept. All say multi-agent supervision is a status-surface problem.
