HARD CONSTRAINTS
- The display shows counts and text only. Approving tool use stays in the terminal; no remote approval endpoint.
- Server is LAN-only, requires a bearer token loaded from .env (never committed, never printed), and rejects unknown event kinds.
- No prompt or code content leaves the machine: hooks send session_id, event kind and timestamp only.
- Display must show a stale marker if /state has not succeeded for 60 s.
- Metrics are defined before data collection in prereg.md and not changed afterward.

DELIVERABLES, IN ORDER
1. ground_truth.md: hook event list and stdin JSON fields confirmed by logging real events to a file for one session; LCD wiring (SCLK, MOSI, CS, EXTCOMIN or software VCOM, 5V/3V3 per breakout); measured baseline agent wait time from 3 days of hook logs.
2. server/: FastAPI + SQLite with /hook, /tap, /state (ETag), /export.csv; pytest for each route.
3. hooks/: settings.json snippet registering Notification, Stop, UserPromptSubmit and PreToolUse hooks that curl /hook in the background with a 2 s timeout so a dead server never blocks Claude Code.
4. firmware/: PlatformIO project, Adafruit_SharpMem, 5 s polling with If-None-Match, partial redraw, stale marker, VCOM at 1 Hz, OTA disabled by default.
5. stand/: a parametric stand (OpenSCAD or CadQuery) at 15 degrees tilt with cable channel.
6. nfc/: tag map (tag id to action), Shortcut export instructions, and a test log of 20 taps with latency.
7. study/: prereg.md, the ABAB schedule, analysis.py computing both metrics per phase with bootstrap intervals.
8. report.md.

BUILT-IN GAP ANALYSIS
Keep GAPS in report.md with VERIFIED / UNVERIFIED / FALSE and evidence for: latency under 10 s from hook to panel; latency from tap to panel; current draw; that the Notification hook fires on permission prompts in your Claude Code version; that the waiting count clears when the user responds; that the stale marker appears when the server is killed; that wait time is lower in display phases than in the ntfy phase; habituation (glance-triggered actions per day trend within display phases). Fill each by running the test.

SELF-QUESTIONS
- Does a session that ends without a Stop event leave the count stuck?
- Does the count double when two Notification events fire for one prompt?
- Is the baseline long enough to see day-to-day variance?
- Am I counting taps that would have happened anyway as glance-triggered?
- What happens on Wi-Fi drop at 3 a.m.?
- Can anyone on the LAN spoof /tap or /hook?

STOP CONDITIONS
Stop and ask if Claude Code hook behavior differs from the docs in a way that breaks the waiting count, or if the user does not want to run the ntfy phase. Stop building features once latency and stale handling pass; the study is the point.

RETURN FORMAT
report.md with a table per phase (days, glance-triggered actions per day, median and p90 agent wait time, intervals), latency and power measurements, the falsifier verdict, GAPS, and the file tree.

steps.title: Ground truth: hooks, display, baseline
steps.goal: Confirm what the hooks actually emit, how the display is driven, and what wait time is today.
steps.prompt: Add a temporary Claude Code hook config that, for Notification, Stop, UserPromptSubmit and PreToolUse, appends the stdin JSON's keys (not values of prompts or tool inputs) plus session_id, hook_event_name and a timestamp to ~/hooklog.jsonl. Run three real sessions including one that asks for a permission and one you abandon. Document which events fire when, whether Notification fires for permission prompts and for idle, and whether an abandoned session ever sends Stop. Leave the logger running 3 days and compute baseline agent wait time: for each Notification, minutes until the next UserPromptSubmit or PreToolUse in the same session. Read the LS027B7DH01 datasheet and the Adafruit Sharp memory breakout guide; record the pinout, voltage, SPI mode and the VCOM toggle requirement (about 1 Hz, via EXTCOMIN pin or software bit). Write ground_truth.md.
steps.expect: ground_truth.md with an event table, three annotated session traces, baseline wait-time median and p90, and the display wiring table.
steps.audit: Confirm no prompt text or tool input made it into hooklog.jsonl (grep for a known prompt string). Fail and fix the logger if it did. Mark any doc claim you could not trigger as UNVERIFIED.

steps.title: State server and hooks
steps.goal: One small LAN endpoint that turns events into display state.
steps.prompt: Write server/ with FastAPI and SQLite. Tables: events(ts, source, session_id, kind, tag). Routes: POST /hook (body: session_id, kind) and POST /tap (body: tag, action), both requiring a bearer token from .env; GET /state returning {now_lines: first 3 non-empty lines of NOW.md, waiting: count, updated: ts} with an ETag hash; GET /export.csv. Waiting logic: a session is waiting after a Notification until its next UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse or Stop; expire waiting after 2 hours so abandoned sessions do not stick. Write hooks/settings.json snippet: each hook runs curl -s -m 2 in the background so Claude Code never blocks. Write pytest cases: double Notification counts once; Stop clears; expiry works; bad token returns 401; NOW.md edits change the ETag. Log every /state fetch with its ETag so step 5 can compute glance windows.
steps.expect: server/ with passing tests, hooks snippet, .env.example with the token name only.
steps.audit: Kill the server and run a Claude Code session; confirm hooks add under 100 ms and no error appears. Fail if any test is skipped. Check .gitignore includes .env before the first commit.

steps.title: Firmware and stand
steps.goal: Show state on the Sharp memory LCD with honest staleness.
steps.prompt: Create a PlatformIO ESP32 project using Adafruit_SharpMem at 400x240. Every 5 s, GET /state with If-None-Match; on 200, redraw: a large waiting count top-right (inverted block when above zero), the three NOW lines word-wrapped below, and a small updated time. On 304 do nothing. Toggle VCOM at 1 Hz from a hardware timer. If no successful response for 60 s, draw a diagonal stale stripe and the last success time. Store Wi-Fi credentials and the token in a secrets.h that is gitignored. Measure current with a USB power meter: idle polling, during redraw, and with Wi-Fi modem sleep enabled. Write a parametric stand in OpenSCAD: 15 degree tilt, pocket for the breakout, cable channel, print-ready STL. Place it where it sits in peripheral vision from the keyboard, not behind the monitor.
steps.expect: firmware that builds, photos or a description of the panel in three states (zero, waiting, stale), current measurements, stand.scad and STL.
steps.audit: Pull the server's network and time how long until the stale stripe appears; fail if over 75 s. Measure hook-to-panel latency 10 times with a phone stopwatch; fail if median exceeds 10 s.

steps.title: NFC tap input
steps.goal: One-tap physical logging that reaches the display.
steps.prompt: Write NTAG213 tags (NFC Tools) for desk (started), water bottle (done-water) and door (leaving). In iOS Shortcuts create one personal automation per tag: When NFC tag is scanned, Get Contents of URL POST to http://<server>/tap with JSON {tag, action} and the bearer header, Run Immediately on, Notify When Run off. Android users: Tasker with an NFC profile and HTTP Request action. Add a /state field last_tap so the panel shows a one-line confirmation for 30 s after a tap. Tap each tag 20 times across a day and log end-to-end latency from tap to panel. Document what happens off-LAN (expect failure) and decide whether to queue taps in the Shortcut or accept loss. Record that decision, because lost taps would otherwise read as no action in the study.
steps.expect: nfc/tagmap.md, shortcut steps, a latency log of 60 taps with median and p90.
steps.audit: Fail if more than 2 of 60 taps are lost while on LAN. Confirm the token is not visible in any screenshot you saved.

steps.title: Pre-register and run the ABAB study
steps.goal: Collect 14 days of evidence that can falsify the idea.
steps.prompt: Write study/prereg.md before day 1: phases A1 days 1-3 baseline (display face down, logging on), B1 days 4-7 display on, C days 8-10 display off with ntfy phone notifications sent by the server on each new waiting session, B2 days 11-14 display on. Metrics: (1) glance-triggered actions per day = taps or UserPromptSubmit events within 2 minutes after a /state change that the device fetched (log fetches server-side); (2) agent wait time per Notification, median and p90. Expected effect, minimum effect worth keeping (for example 25% lower median wait than phase C), and the falsifier from the dive: glance-triggered actions near zero by week two and wait time not lower than phase C. Write analysis.py producing per-phase tables with bootstrap 95% intervals and a daily trend plot for habituation. Then run the 14 days; record deviations in a log.
steps.expect: prereg.md committed before day 1 (git timestamp), 14 days of events, analysis.py output.
steps.audit: Check the prereg commit predates the first study event. Fail if metric definitions changed after day 1; if they did, report both versions.

steps.title: Validate against oracles and write the gap report
steps.goal: Score the falsifier and list what is still unproven.
steps.prompt: Run analysis.py on /export.csv. Report per phase: days, glance-triggered actions per day, median and p90 wait time, intervals. Compare B1 and B2 against A1 and against C. Score habituation as the slope of daily glance-triggered actions within B phases. State the falsifier verdict: fired (display not better than phone notification and habituating), did not fire, or inconclusive (intervals overlap). Include latency and power measurements and the stale test. Have a second person sit at the desk for one hour without instructions and record whether they can say how many agents are waiting. Write report.md with a GAPS list: each claim VERIFIED, UNVERIFIED or FALSE with evidence, and the top three gaps fixed or with reasons. End with a keep, change or retire recommendation for the device.
steps.expect: report.md with phase table, verdict, measurements, second-person result and GAPS.
steps.audit: Recompute two numbers in the table by hand from the CSV. Fail if the verdict claims a win while intervals overlap with phase C.

ambient-executive-function.gap_audit_prompt: You are auditing an ambient executive-function display build: ESP32 + Sharp memory LCD, FastAPI state server, Claude Code hooks, NFC taps, 14-day ABAB study. Inputs: ground_truth.md, server/, hooks/, firmware/, nfc/, study/, report.md, events export. 1) Enumerate claims: latency targets met, stale marker works, waiting count correct, no prompt content logged, token never committed, metrics pre-registered, wait time improved versus the phone-notification phase. 2) Re-verify each: run the pytest suite; grep git history for the token name with a value; grep the events DB for any free text; kill the server and time the stale marker; replay the CSV through analysis.py and recompute the phase table; check the prereg commit time against the first event. Mark VERIFIED, UNVERIFIED or FALSE with output. 3) Look for silent failures: sessions stuck as waiting, duplicate Notification events, taps lost off-LAN counted as no action, days missing from the export. 4) Rank gaps by effect on the verdict. 5) Fix the top three and rerun. 6) Report what you could not fix and why, and whether the falsifier verdict changes.
self_questions: Does Notification fire for permission prompts in my installed Claude Code version, or only for idle waits?
Do abandoned sessions without a Stop event inflate the waiting count?
Are glance-triggered actions distinguishable from actions I would have taken anyway, given the baseline rate?
Is the Hawthorne effect from logging itself captured by the A1 baseline?
Is the ntfy comparison phase fair (same events, same timing)?
Does the panel ever show stale data without the stale marker?
Is VCOM toggling, or will the LCD degrade over weeks?
Can a device on my LAN spoof /tap or /hook without the token?
Did any prompt text, file path or tool input leave the machine through a hook?
Is NOW.md actually maintained daily, or is the panel showing week-old lines?
What is the current draw, and does it matter if the device is USB-powered?
validation_oracles: Event logs: analysis.py on the SQLite export gives per-phase wait time and glance-triggered actions with bootstrap intervals; the display phases are compared to the ntfy phone-notification phase.
Stopwatch or screen recording: 10 hook-to-panel and 60 tap-to-panel latency measurements, median under 10 s.
USB power meter: idle and redraw current recorded.
Kill test: the stale stripe appears within 75 s of stopping the server.
A second person at the desk for an hour can state the waiting count without instruction.
Git history: prereg.md committed before the first study event.
failure_modes: Stuck count. Tell: the panel shows waiting sessions that are closed. Fix: clear on PreToolUse and Stop, expire after 2 hours.
Blocking hooks. Tell: Claude Code feels slow or errors when the server is down. Fix: background curl with -m 2, never fail the hook.
Habituation. Tell: glance-triggered actions decline daily within B phases. Fix: change only on state change (inverted block), consider brief motion; if it persists, the falsifier fired.
Confounded result. Tell: wait time drops from A1 to B1 but B1 equals C. Fix: report that the gain comes from any notification, not the ambient display.
Silent staleness. Tell: correct-looking counts that do not change. Fix: stale stripe and last-success time.
Leaky logging. Tell: prompt text in the events table. Fix: hooks send only session_id and kind.
Spoofable endpoint. Tell: requests without a token succeed. Fix: bearer token check and LAN binding.
ambient-executive-function.agent_direction: Start with step 1's hook logger and the datasheet; it is cheap and decides the waiting logic. Use Python FastAPI and SQLite for the server, PlatformIO for firmware, OpenSCAD for the stand. Spawn a sub-agent for the stand model and another for firmware while you build the server, since they only share the /state contract; write that JSON contract first and hand it to both. Cache the hooklog and the exports. Never print or commit the bearer token or Wi-Fi password; load them from .env and a gitignored secrets.h. Stop and ask the user before editing their global Claude Code settings.json (show the snippet instead), before flashing hardware, and before starting the 14-day study, since it needs their cooperation. Return: ground_truth.md, server/ with tests, hooks/ snippet, firmware/, stand/, nfc/, study/prereg.md and analysis.py, report.md with the falsifier verdict.

sketch-to-production.mission: Running this system takes one hand-drawn character from a Procreate kit-bash sheet to a rigged, animated, rendered 3D shot using Jon Finger's chain (Procreate, Magnific style transfer, 3DAI Studio or Hunyuan3D-2, Move AI mocap, render) with Kling as a fallback for 2D-to-video. It is for an indie creator who wants to know if the 'under an hour, about 45 minutes per asset' claim holds and where the chain breaks. Done means a timed log for each stage, a mesh that passes technical checks (manifold, polycount, UVs, valid glTF), a retargeted mocap clip without foot sliding, a render, and a gap report naming the stages that needed manual cleanup.

deeper_not_bigger.professional_would: A character TD would refuse to send a single loose sketch to image-to-3D. They would draw an orthographic turnaround (front, side, back at the same scale) or, like Jon Finger, a kit-bash sheet of separate parts, then check the generated mesh for topology, scale and pivots before rigging. They would retopologize to an animation-friendly quad mesh, bake the generated texture onto clean UVs, and rig with a standard skeleton so mocap retargets. They would also time each stage honestly, including failed generations and cleanup, and check license terms for every tool before calling the asset production-ready.
deeper_not_bigger.rawest_material:
- Jon Finger's own description (via chatgptricks): parts sketched as a kit-bash sheet in Procreate, made to look 3D with Magnific, converted with 3D AI Studio, assembled into a humanoid, Move AI performance on top, Cinema 4D render.
- Tencent Hunyuan3D-2 GitHub repo and model card (shape stage then texture stage), and its LICENSE file, which restricts some territories.
- Move AI export docs (FBX/BVH skeleton naming, frame rate).
- Kling motion brush docs (up to 5 subjects with drawn paths) and Magnific's creativity/resemblance settings.
- Blender manual: Rigify, QuadriFlow remesh, bake, the glTF 2.0 exporter.
- Khronos glTF-Validator.
- Your own sketch files at full resolution, not screenshots.
deeper_not_bigger.methods_tools: Procreate (export PNG per part at 2048 px on white), Magnific AI with resemblance high and creativity low to keep silhouettes, Hunyuan3D-2 run locally (python with the shape and paint pipelines) or the 3DAI Studio web app, Blender 4.x headless via bpy for import, scale normalization, merge, decimate or QuadriFlow, Smart UV project and texture bake, Rigify or Mixamo auto-rig, retargeting Move AI FBX with the Rokoko retargeting add-on or Blender's built-in constraints, trimesh for watertight and polycount checks, glTF-Validator for export, FFmpeg for assembly, and a stage-timing CSV.
deeper_not_bigger.external_proof: Technical oracles: trimesh reports watertight meshes with a triangle count under budget; glTF-Validator reports zero errors; the GLB opens in a third-party viewer (Babylon.js sandbox or three.js editor) with textures; Blender renders the animated shot headless without errors. Motion oracle: foot contacts stay within 1 cm of the floor in contact frames. Time oracle: a stopwatch log per stage including failed attempts. Human oracle: an animator or a viewer judges whether the result still matches the sketch.
deeper_not_bigger.rewritten_prompt: Take my Procreate character from sketch to a rendered animated shot and measure every stage. Do not start from one loose drawing: help me produce a kit-bash sheet of separate parts plus a front and side view at the same scale, as Jon Finger did. Run each part through Magnific with high resemblance and low creativity, then to 3D through Hunyuan3D-2 (local, shape then texture) and, as a comparison, 3DAI Studio. In Blender headless: normalize scale to meters, set pivots, assemble the humanoid, remesh with QuadriFlow to under 30k quads, project UVs, bake the generated texture, rig with Rigify, and retarget a Move AI capture of me. Check with trimesh (watertight, polycount), glTF-Validator (zero errors), and a foot-contact script (contact frames within 1 cm of the floor). Render 5 seconds at 24 fps and assemble with FFmpeg. Keep a CSV of start and end time per stage, including failed generations and manual fixes, so the '45 minutes per asset' claim is tested. Read the Hunyuan3D-2 license and each service's commercial terms and list restrictions. Finish with a gap report: which stages needed manual work, total time, and whether the asset is game-ready or only render-ready.

sketch-to-production.one_shot:
ROLE AND STANCE
You are a character technical director running an AI-assisted asset pipeline. You care about whether the asset survives rigging, animation and export, not whether a turntable looks good. You time everything and count failed attempts. You treat 'under an hour' as a claim to measure.

CONTEXT
- Jon Finger's chain (chatgptricks post): sketch parts as a kit-bash sheet in Procreate, Magnific AI style transfer to make them look 3D, 3D AI Studio to convert to meshes, assemble a humanoid, Move AI motion capture of his own performance, Cinema 4D render. He called it 'a little experiment'.
- Hunyuan3D-2 (nick_saraev): free image-to-3D, Generate Shape then Generate Textured Shape; open weights on GitHub.
- Kling motion brush (realrileybrown): select up to 5 subjects in a still and draw motion paths; a 2D-to-video fallback when 3D fails.
- AI rotoscoping (iamfesq): segmentation mask to composite yourself into the scene.
- The dive's claim: about 45 minutes per asset from napkin to animated render.

HARD CONSTRAINTS
- Every stage writes its output to stages/NN_name/ with the exact settings used and a row in timing.csv (stage, start, end, attempts, manual_fix_minutes, notes).
- Mesh budget: under 30k quads after retopology, single material, 2048 px texture.
- Scale in meters, character about 1.7 m, feet on Z=0, forward -Y.
- No commercial-use claim until each tool's license and plan terms are recorded in licenses.md (Hunyuan3D-2's license has territory restrictions; Magnific, 3DAI Studio, Move AI and Kling terms vary by plan).
- Do not upload other people's art or likeness.

DELIVERABLES, IN ORDER
1. ground_truth.md: tool versions and plans, license notes, the original sketch files, and a reference timing goal.
2. stages/01_sheet: kit-bash parts sheet plus front and side views exported as separate 2048 px PNGs on white.
3. stages/02_magnific: each part with recorded resemblance and creativity settings.
4. stages/03_mesh: Hunyuan3D-2 meshes and 3DAI Studio meshes for the same parts, with a comparison table (triangles, watertight, visual fidelity score 1-5).
5. stages/04_assembly: Blender .blend and a headless script assemble.py that imports, scales, sets pivots, joins, remeshes with QuadriFlow, UV-projects and bakes.
6. stages/05_rig: Rigify rig with weights; test poses.
7. stages/06_mocap: Move AI capture exported to FBX, retargeted; foot-contact report.
8. stages/07_render: 5-second 24 fps render, FFmpeg-assembled MP4, GLB export validated.
9. fallback/: if 3D fails, a Kling motion-brush clip from the Magnific image, labeled as 2D.
10. report.md.

BUILT-IN GAP ANALYSIS
Maintain GAPS in report.md. For each claim mark VERIFIED, UNVERIFIED or FALSE with evidence: total time under 60 minutes; parts converted without manual mesh repair; Hunyuan3D-2 versus 3DAI Studio fidelity; mesh watertight after assembly; weights deform without candy-wrapping at elbows and knees; mocap retarget without foot sliding; GLB valid; commercial use allowed. Run the checks; list what is left with the next action.

SELF-QUESTIONS
- Did a single sketch angle produce a plausible back side, or did the model invent one?
- Did Magnific change the design (extra details, different proportions) and did I accept drift without noticing?
- Are the generated meshes one shell or many intersecting shells?
- Is the texture baked onto my new UVs or still on the generator's atlas?
- Is the timing honest, including generation queues and retries?
- Would this asset survive a game engine import, or is it render-only?

STOP CONDITIONS
Stop and report if image-to-3D fails on more than half of the parts after 3 attempts each; produce the Kling fallback and document why. Stop before any paid upgrade or upload of identifiable likeness; ask the user.

RETURN FORMAT
report.md: a timing table per stage with attempts and manual minutes, the mesh comparison table, validator outputs, the foot-contact result, license table, verdict (game-ready / render-ready / failed), GAPS, and links to the MP4 and GLB.

steps.title: Ground truth: tools, licenses, source sketch
steps.goal: Pin tool versions, terms and the raw sketch before generating anything.
steps.prompt: List every tool in the chain (Procreate, Magnific AI, 3DAI Studio, Hunyuan3D-2, Move AI, Blender, Kling) with the version or plan the user has. Clone Tencent's Hunyuan3D-2 repo, read README and LICENSE, and record the territory restrictions and commercial terms verbatim. For each paid service record what the current plan allows for commercial use and output ownership, with the URL of the terms page and the date read. Collect the user's original sketch files at full resolution. Write the 45-minute claim as a hypothesis and create timing.csv with headers stage, start, end, attempts, manual_fix_minutes, notes. Check whether a local GPU can run Hunyuan3D-2 (record VRAM and the repo's stated minimum) or whether the web UI must be used. Note that Jon Finger rendered in Cinema 4D; decide whether Blender replaces it and say so. Write ground_truth.md and licenses.md.
steps.expect: ground_truth.md, licenses.md with quoted terms and dates, timing.csv header, sketches in stages/00_source.
steps.audit: Fail if any license row says 'probably fine' or lacks a source URL and date. Mark the tool UNVERIFIED for commercial use instead.

steps.title: Kit-bash sheet and turnaround
steps.goal: Give the image-to-3D stage inputs it can succeed with.
steps.prompt: From the source sketch, produce in Procreate (or describe exactly for the user to draw) a kit-bash sheet like Jon Finger's: head, torso, each arm, each leg, hands and props drawn separately, front-facing, consistent scale, on white, with clear silhouettes and no overlapping parts. Add a front and side view of the assembled character at the same height. Export each part as a 2048 px PNG with a transparent or white background. Then run each part through Magnific with high resemblance and low creativity; record the slider values and prompt per part. Compare each Magnific output to its sketch with an overlay at 50% opacity and note any added or removed features. Keep part names consistent across files (head, torso, arm_L, arm_R) so later scripts can find them.
steps.expect: stages/01_sheet with 8-12 part PNGs and two views; stages/02_magnific with outputs, settings.json and an overlay note per part.
steps.audit: Fail any part whose Magnific silhouette deviates visibly from the sketch (new limbs, changed proportions); rerun with lower creativity. Log time and attempts.

steps.title: Image to 3D, two generators
steps.goal: Convert parts to meshes and compare Hunyuan3D-2 with 3DAI Studio.
steps.prompt: For each Magnific part, generate a mesh with Hunyuan3D-2 locally (shape pipeline, then paint pipeline for texture; record seed, steps and octree resolution) and with 3DAI Studio's web tool. Export GLB or OBJ. Write mesh_check.py using trimesh: triangle count, number of connected bodies, is_watertight, bounding box, and texture presence. Produce a comparison table per part: generator, triangles, bodies, watertight, fidelity to the sketch scored 1-5 by overlaying a front render on the sketch. Pick the better mesh per part with a reason. Log generation time and queue time separately in timing.csv. If Hunyuan3D-2 is run locally, also record GPU time per part so the cost of the free route is visible. Keep every rejected mesh with its seed; do not overwrite.
steps.expect: stages/03_mesh with two meshes per part, mesh_check.py output and a comparison table.
steps.audit: Fail a mesh with more than 3 bodies or that is non-watertight where it should be solid; retry with a cleaner input image, then mark for manual repair. Stop per the stop condition if more than half the parts fail after 3 attempts.

steps.title: Assemble, retopologize, bake
steps.goal: Make one clean animation-ready mesh in Blender headless.
steps.prompt: Write assemble.py for blender -b -P: import chosen part meshes, scale so total height is 1.7 m, place feet at Z=0 facing -Y, position parts using the front and side views as reference planes, join into one object, voxel remesh at 1 cm to fuse shells, then QuadriFlow remesh to a target of 25k faces. Duplicate the original textured parts as a bake source. Smart UV project the new mesh with 0.02 island margin, bake diffuse from the source with cage extrusion 0.02 to a 2048 px image, assign a single material. Save .blend and export GLB. Run mesh_check.py and Khronos glTF-Validator on the GLB. Record the face count before and after QuadriFlow and how long each Blender operation took.
steps.expect: assembly .blend, assemble.py, character.glb, validator report with zero errors, mesh_check output.
steps.audit: Render front and side views and overlay them on the sketch views. Fail if the texture has black bake holes over 2% of the surface or validator errors exist; fix cage distance or UVs and rerun.

steps.title: Rig, mocap, retarget
steps.goal: Drive the character with the user's own performance.
steps.prompt: Add a Rigify human metarig, fit bones to the mesh using the side view, generate the rig and bind with automatic weights. Test 6 poses (arms up, squat, twist, walk contact, fist, head turn) and note candy-wrapping or tearing. Capture a 5-second Move AI performance of the user (single or multi-camera as their plan allows), export FBX at 24 fps, and retarget to the Rigify rig with the Rokoko retargeting add-on or a bone-mapping script. Write foot_contact.py: detect frames where foot velocity is under 2 cm per frame and report foot height and horizontal drift in those frames. Confirm the Move AI frame rate matches the scene frame rate before retargeting; a mismatch causes sliding that no IK fix hides. Log manual weight-paint minutes in timing.csv.
steps.expect: rigged .blend, pose test renders, retargeted action, foot_contact report.
steps.audit: Fail if foot height in contact frames exceeds 1 cm or drift exceeds 2 cm per contact; fix with a root-height offset or IK foot locks, rerun the script.

steps.title: Render and fallback
steps.goal: Produce the final shot and a 2D fallback for comparison.
steps.prompt: Light the scene with a three-point setup, render 120 frames at 24 fps in Eevee at 1920x1080 headless (blender -b scene.blend -a), and assemble with FFmpeg: ffmpeg -framerate 24 -i frame_%04d.png -c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p -crf 18 shot.mp4. Export a final GLB with the animation and validate it again; open it in the Babylon.js sandbox or three.js editor and confirm the animation plays and the texture is not missing. Log render time per frame in timing.csv. As a fallback and comparison, feed the best Magnific image into Kling, use motion brush on up to 5 regions to animate a similar action, and save it labeled 2D. If AI rotoscoping of the user is wanted, segment the user's video with a segmentation model and composite the character beside them.
steps.expect: shot.mp4, animated GLB passing validation, a third-party viewer screenshot, Kling fallback clip.
steps.audit: Check shot.mp4 with ffprobe for 120 frames at 24 fps. Fail if the GLB animation does not play in the third-party viewer.

steps.title: Validate against oracles and write the gap report
steps.goal: Test the 45-minute claim and the production-ready claim.
steps.prompt: Sum timing.csv per stage and total, separating machine time, queue time and manual minutes. Compare to the 45-minute claim, and compute what the total would be on a second asset reusing the scripts (exclude one-time setup like installing Hunyuan3D-2). Rerun mesh_check.py, glTF-Validator and foot_contact.py and paste outputs. Ask one person (ideally an animator) to compare the render to the original sketch and score likeness 1-5 and motion quality 1-5. Classify the asset: game-ready (valid GLB, under budget, clean rig), render-ready (looks right, fails technical checks), or failed. Write report.md with GAPS: each claim VERIFIED, UNVERIFIED or FALSE with evidence, plus the three most expensive stages and what would shorten them next time. State plainly whether the dive's under-an-hour claim held for this asset, and with how many attempts.

sketch-to-production.gap_audit_prompt: You are auditing a sketch-to-animated-3D asset produced with Procreate, Magnific, Hunyuan3D-2 or 3DAI Studio, Blender, Move AI and optionally Kling. self_questions: Did I give image-to-3D separate parts and orthographic views, or one perspective sketch it had to guess from?
Did Magnific's style transfer drift the design, and did I check with an overlay?
Is the Hunyuan3D-2 license compatible with the user's country and intended use?
Are meshes fused into one shell, or will intersecting parts tear when rigged?

foot_contact.py shows foot height within 1 cm and drift under 2 cm in contact frames.
Stopwatch-based timing.csv totals versus the 45-minute claim, with retries and manual minutes included.
An animator or independent viewer scores likeness to the sketch and motion quality.
failure_modes: Invented back side. Tell: the back of the mesh is lumpy or mirrors the front. Fix: supply a side and back view or generate parts separately.
Style drift. Tell: Magnific adds features the sketch lacks. Fix: high resemblance, low creativity, overlay check.
Multi-shell mesh. Tell: trimesh counts many bodies, rig tears. Fix: voxel remesh before QuadriFlow.
Lost texture. Tell: black or smeared bake. Fix: correct cage extrusion, island margin, re-bake.
Foot sliding. Tell: drift in contact frames. Fix: root offset, IK foot locks, matched frame rate.
Time claim inflated. Tell: totals exclude queues and retries. Fix: log every attempt.
License surprise. Tell: commercial use blocked by plan or territory. Fix: record terms before production use.

They would smooth landmarks with a One Euro filter, handle tracking loss gracefully, and make the piece boot itself after a power cut. They would playtest with strangers and change the mapping until the interaction is legible in 10 seconds.

interactive-installations.one_shot:
ROLE AND STANCE
You are a creative technologist delivering an interactive installation to a gallery. You optimize for legibility, latency and uptime, in that order. You assume the room is too bright, the visitors do unexpected things, and the power will be cut.

CONTEXT
- pala3d's DATA CONTROL: NASA and CERN datasets turned into particle structures, body-controlled via Kinect through TouchDesigner into Unreal Engine, explicitly human-made.
- neles0n using @blankensmithing's MediaPipe plugin in TouchDesigner (github torinmb/mediapipe-touchdesigner): webcam body and hand tracking without a Kinect.
- Physical references in the dive: speaker-driven soap-film cymatics (vibra.genix; ignore its health and '4D' claims, keep the standing-wave visual) and Aedas' Al Bahar Towers, a sun-responsive mashrabiya façade reported to halve cooling load. Both are input-to-form mappings worth borrowing for interaction design.
- The dive's claim: webcam, TouchDesigner and a $200 projector give gallery-quality interaction for under $500 in hardware.

HARD CONSTRAINTS
- Latency budget: median motion-to-photon under 100 ms.
- Frame rate at least 30 fps at output resolution for 8 hours.
- Must cold-boot into the piece without a keyboard (OS auto-login, TouchDesigner in Perform mode via startup script).
- No recording or storage of visitor video or landmarks beyond aggregated counts; post a notice if any camera is used.
- Respect TouchDesigner license tiers: non-commercial caps output at 1280x1280 and excludes paid commercial work; record which tier is used.
- No liquid near powered speakers for any cymatics element.

DELIVERABLES, IN ORDER
1. ground_truth.md: hardware list with prices, TouchDesigner build and license tier, MediaPipe plugin version and which models run, webcam fps at chosen resolution, projector throw ratio and lumens, room measurements and ambient lux.
2. tracking.toe network section: plugin outputs to CHOPs, One Euro filter, derived features (hand speed, arm span, centroid, person count), tracking-loss handling (fade over 1 s, never snap).
3. visual: GPU particle system mapped from features; a data mode that loads a NASA Exoplanet Archive CSV (orbital period, radius, distance) or a CERN open-data event table as particle positions and lets hands sweep through it.
4. attract mode when person count is 0 for 20 s.
5. optional ue/: Unreal project receiving OSC on a fixed port, used only if the TouchDesigner look fails a stated criterion.
6. ops/: startup script, auto-login notes, watchdog that restarts TouchDesigner if the frame-time log stops, frame-time CSV logger.
7. tests/: latency protocol and results, soak log, playtest sheet.
8. report.md.

BUILT-IN GAP ANALYSIS
Maintain GAPS in report.md marking VERIFIED, UNVERIFIED or FALSE with evidence: latency under 100 ms; 30 fps for 8 hours; tracking under gallery lighting (dim room, projector light on the visitor); behavior with 3+ people; legibility (strangers interact within 15 s); total hardware cost under $500; projector brightness sufficient at measured ambient lux; data mode faithful to the source dataset (spot-check 10 rows). Fill each gap by testing; list the rest with the next action.

SELF-QUESTIONS
- What does the piece do when two people overlap or one leaves mid-gesture?
- Does projector light on the visitor's body break MediaPipe tracking?
- Is latency dominated by the webcam, the model, TouchDesigner or the projector's input lag?
- Would a visitor know what to do without a sign?
- Does the data mode mean anything, or is it decoration with a NASA label?
- What happens at hour 6 when the GPU is hot?

STOP CONDITIONS
Stop and ask the user before buying hardware, before using a commercial TouchDesigner license, and if tracking fails under the room's lighting after trying a different camera position and the heavy model. Do not add Unreal unless TouchDesigner fails a written criterion.

RETURN FORMAT
report.md with: BOM table and total, latency results (median, p90), soak summary, playtest table, license notes, GAPS with statuses, and the file tree.

steps.title: Ground truth: room, hardware, licenses
steps.goal: Measure the space and confirm what the tools actually allow before building.
steps.prompt: Measure the installation wall (width, height), the maximum projector distance, and ambient light with a phone lux meter at the wall and where viewers will stand, at the time of day the piece will run. From the projector spec sheet, compute image width = distance / throw ratio and check it fills the wall; estimate brightness on the wall as ANSI lumens / area in square meters and compare to ambient lux (aim for at least 5x ambient). Install TouchDesigner and record the build and license tier; note the non-commercial 1280x1280 cap and commercial restrictions. Install torinmb/mediapipe-touchdesigner, record its version and which models (pose, hands, face) run, and measure webcam fps at 720p and 1080p. List hardware with real prices and links. If a Kinect is considered, check whether the model is still sold and supported. Write ground_truth.md.
steps.expect: ground_truth.md with room numbers, throw and brightness math, license tier, plugin version, measured fps and a priced hardware list.
steps.audit: Recompute the throw and brightness math independently. Fail if any price is a guess without a link, or if the license tier conflicts with the intended use; flag it for the user.

steps.title: Tracking layer with filtering and loss handling
steps.goal: Turn webcam frames into stable, meaningful features.
steps.prompt: In TouchDesigner, bring the MediaPipe plugin's pose (33 landmarks) and hand (21 landmarks per hand) outputs into CHOPs. Apply a One Euro filter per channel (start with min cutoff 1.0 and beta 0.007; implement in a Script CHOP if no built-in exists) and tune by recording jitter while standing still and lag during a fast wave. Derive features: hand speed (m/s in normalized units), arm span, body centroid, height of the highest wrist, person count. When tracking drops, hold the last values and fade influence to zero over 1 second; never snap. Test with 1, 2 and 3 people and with someone walking through the frame. Note which person the plugin tracks when several are present and whether that switches mid-gesture. Record CPU and GPU load and the plugin's reported inference time per frame.
steps.expect: A tracking network section with filtered feature CHOPs, a jitter versus lag tuning note, and multi-person test notes.
steps.audit: Plot raw versus filtered wrist x over 10 s still and 10 s waving. Fail if still jitter exceeds 1% of frame width or waving lag looks worse than 3 frames; retune beta and min cutoff.

steps.title: Visual mapping and data mode
steps.goal: Build a visual whose response to the body is obvious and whose data mode is faithful.
steps.prompt: Build a GPU particle system (particlesGPU component or a GLSL TOP with instanced geometry) at the projector's native resolution, within the license cap. Map features: hand speed drives emission and turbulence, arm span drives field width, wrist height drives color temperature, and person count spawns separate flows. Borrow the cymatics idea for an audio mode: an audio spectrum CHOP sets standing-wave patterns, without any liquid near speakers. Add a data mode: load a NASA Exoplanet Archive CSV (pl_orbper, pl_rade, sy_dist) or a CERN Open Data event table, map columns to particle position, size and color with a documented scale, and let hands push particles aside and release them back. Write the mapping in a table. Add an attract mode that animates slowly when no one is tracked for 20 s.
steps.expect: A visual network, a mapping table, a data mode with a documented column-to-attribute scale, and an attract mode.
steps.audit: Spot-check 10 dataset rows: their particles must sit where the mapping says. Fail if fps drops under 30 at output resolution; reduce particle count or resolution and record the trade-off.

steps.title: Latency measurement and optional Unreal
steps.goal: Measure motion-to-photon latency and decide whether Unreal is needed.
steps.prompt: Set up a latency test: a visible LED or phone flashlight held in the hand, and a TouchDesigner element that flips color when wrist speed crosses a threshold. Film the hand and the projection in one frame at 240 fps. For 20 trials, count frames from the start of the hand's motion to the projection change; convert to ms. Break latency down: webcam exposure and USB, plugin inference time, TouchDesigner cook time (Perform CHOP), projector input lag (spec or game mode). If the median exceeds 100 ms, try 720p input, the lite pose model, and the projector's low-latency mode. Write a criterion for adding Unreal (for example, a specific lighting or scale look TouchDesigner cannot reach at 30 fps). Only if it is met, send features over OSC (OSC Out CHOP to a fixed port) to an Unreal Blueprint and re-measure latency end to end.
steps.expect: tests/latency.md with 20 trials, median and p90, a breakdown, and a written Unreal decision.
steps.audit: Recount 5 trials from the video independently. Fail if median exceeds 100 ms after the three mitigations; report the bottleneck rather than hiding it.

steps.title: Unattended operation and soak test
steps.goal: Make the piece boot itself and survive 8 hours.
steps.prompt: Write a startup script that launches TouchDesigner with the project in Perform mode on the projector output, set OS auto-login and disable sleep, screen savers and update reboots during exhibition hours. Add a frame-time logger writing timestamp, fps, GPU temperature if available, and person count to CSV every 10 s. Add a watchdog (a small Python or PowerShell script) that restarts TouchDesigner if the CSV has not updated in 60 s. Pull the power plug and confirm the piece returns without a keyboard. Then run an 8-hour soak with the room lit as for the show, with people walking past at intervals or a looping video of people played to the webcam. Do not record or store visitor video; log only aggregates.
steps.expect: ops/ scripts, a cold-boot test note, and an 8-hour CSV with summary stats (min fps, crashes, restarts).
steps.audit: Fail if fps drops below 30 for more than 1% of samples, if any restart was needed, or if the cold boot required input. Fix and rerun the affected part of the soak.

steps.title: Validate against oracles and write the gap report
steps.goal: Prove legibility, cost and stability with outside evidence.
steps.prompt: Run a playtest with 10 people who have not seen the piece. Give no instructions and no sign. Time from entering the space to their first intentional interaction, and ask one question afterward: what did your body control? Record answers verbatim. Run the playtest under show lighting with the projector at its final position, and note any visitor who got bored or left within 30 seconds. Sum the hardware receipts against the $500 claim, listing anything already owned separately. Compile latency, soak and playtest results. Write report.md with a GAPS list marking each claim VERIFIED, UNVERIFIED or FALSE with evidence: latency, fps, cold boot, legibility, multi-person behavior, data-mode faithfulness, cost, license fit. Fix the top three gaps that block a gallery night and rerun their tests. List what remains with the next action.
steps.expect: report.md with a playtest table, BOM total, latency and soak summaries, GAPS and fixes.
steps.audit: Fail if fewer than 7 of 10 strangers interacted intentionally within 15 s and the report does not propose a mapping change. Check every number against its source file.

interactive-installations.gap_audit_prompt: You are auditing a body-reactive installation built with MediaPipe in TouchDesigner, optional Kinect and Unreal, and a projector. Inputs: ground_truth.md, the .toe project, ops/, tests/, report.md, receipts. 1) Enumerate claims: latency median and p90, 30 fps over 8 hours, cold-boot behavior, multi-person handling, legibility, data-mode faithfulness, hardware under $500, license tier fits the use. 2) Re-verify: recount latency from 5 video trials, recompute soak stats from the CSV, pull power and time the recovery, spot-check 10 data rows against particle positions, re-sum receipts, compare output resolution to the license cap. Mark each VERIFIED, UNVERIFIED or FALSE with evidence. 3) Look for silent failures: watchdog that never fired because the logger also died, tracking-loss snaps, attract mode that never triggers, visitor video being written to disk. 4) Rank gaps by risk to an opening night. 5) Fix the top three now and rerun their tests. 6) Report what you could not fix and why.
self_questions: Does projector light falling on visitors break MediaPipe tracking in the real room?
What is the latency split between webcam, inference, TouchDesigner and the projector?
Do strangers understand the mapping without a sign, and what did they think they controlled?
Does the piece handle three overlapping people without flicker?
Is the One Euro filter tuned for both stillness and fast gestures?
Is the output resolution inside the TouchDesigner license tier I am using?
Does the data mode faithfully show the NASA or CERN data, or just borrow the label?
Will the piece come back after a power cut with nobody there?
Is any visitor video or landmark data stored?
Does the $500 total include the computer, cables, mounts and a spare webcam?
Is Unreal justified by a written criterion, or added because the post used it?
validation_oracles: 240 fps phone video of 20 trials: median motion-to-photon latency under 100 ms, recountable from the footage.
8-hour soak CSV: fps at or above 30 for 99% of samples, zero unrecovered crashes, cold boot after power pull without input.
Playtest with 10 strangers: at least 7 interact intentionally within 15 s and can say what their body controlled.
Purchase receipts summed against the $500 hardware claim.
Spot-check of 10 dataset rows against rendered particle positions.
failure_modes: Tracking collapses under projector light. Tell: landmarks jump when the visitor is lit. Fix: move the camera off-axis, use the heavy model, add IR light with an IR webcam.
Laggy feel. Tell: visitors wave repeatedly. Fix: measure, then drop input resolution, use the lite model, enable projector game mode.
Illegible mapping. Tell: strangers stand still or ask what to do. Fix: one dominant mapping (hand speed to motion), stronger response, attract mode that demonstrates it.
Snapping on tracking loss. Tell: visual jumps when someone leaves. Fix: hold and fade over 1 s.
Overnight death. Tell: black screen in the morning. Fix: watchdog on the logger, disabled updates and sleep.
License violation. Tell: commercial show on a non-commercial key or output over 1280x1280. Fix: buy the right tier or lower resolution.
interactive-installations.agent_direction: Start with the room and license checks; they can invalidate the plan before any patching. TouchDesigner networks are binary .toe files, so write Python (td module) scripts and Script CHOPs where possible and describe node chains in text so they can be reviewed. Use a sub-agent for the startup, watchdog and logging scripts, which are independent of the visual. Cache the dataset CSVs and their column mapping. The latency test and playtest need a human; prepare protocols and sheets, then ask the user to run them and return the video and notes. Stop and ask before buying hardware, switching license tiers, or adding Unreal. Never store visitor video. Return: ground_truth.md, the .toe project with scripts, ops/, tests/latency.md, soak CSV, playtest sheet, report.md with GAPS.

ai-video-production.mission: Running this system produces one finished 60-90 second video made by one person with AI tools: a Claude-written script and shot list, base footage from Runway (Gen-3 Alpha, video-to-video, non-linear keyframe canvas) and Kling (motion brush on up to 5 subjects), optional Veo or Sora shots, an AI-rotoscoped insert of the creator, a screen-recorded segment from OpenScreen, and a final edit with sound. It is for a solo creator testing the '$30 a month replaces a production team' claim. Done means a ledger of every generation with credits and cost, a continuity check by a second person, a delivered file that passes platform specs, and a gap report on where the tools still needed a human.

deeper_not_bigger.professional_would: A producer would start with a script, a shot list and a continuity bible (character reference sheet, wardrobe, palette, lens and lighting per scene) before generating a frame, because AI video fails mostly on consistency between shots. They would pick the tool per shot by what it controls: Kling's motion brush for directed subject motion, Runway video-to-video when a real performance must drive the shot, a keyframe pair on Runway's canvas when start and end frames matter. They would budget by cost per usable second, counting rejected generations, and spend real effort on sound and the edit. They would check commercial rights per plan and label AI content where platforms require it.

deeper_not_bigger.rewritten_prompt: Produce one 60-90 second video with me as a one-person studio, and measure what it really costs. Before any generation: write the script, a numbered shot list with shot type, duration and the tool chosen for each shot with a reason (Kling motion brush for directed subject motion, Runway video-to-video when my real performance drives it, Runway's keyframe canvas when start and end frames matter, Veo or Sora only if available to me), and a continuity bible: character reference sheet, wardrobe, palette, lighting and lens per scene.
